[160] Societal security in an uncertain world Recommendation from the Ministry of Justice and Public Security on October 16, 2020, approved by the Cabinet on the same day

[161] Introduction 1.1 The Government's policy for societal security The Government will base its policy on society's and individual's need for security

[162] Ensuring the safety of citizens is one of the state's most important tasks

[163] The government is working to strengthen society's ability to prevent crises and to handle serious incidents through comprehensive and coordinated work on societal security

[164] This White Paper presents the government's policy in the field of social security in a four-year perspective

[165] This is the second social security announcement under the Solberg government

[166] Previous message, Message

[167] St. 10 (2016–2017) Risk in a safe society, Recommendation

[168] St. (2016–2017), had a main focus on emergency preparedness, and the government has worked purposefully over the past seven years to strengthen central emergency preparedness capacities

[169] Emergency networks have been developed, and have a coverage rate of approximately 86 percent of the land area and close to 100 percent of the population

[170] The first of 16 new rescue helicopters has been put into service, and the rest will be in place during the

[171] The new rescue helicopters, which have been named SAR Queen, have far greater range, greater speed and better ability to operate in bad weather compared to the outgoing Sea King helicopters

[172] In the fall of 2019, the National Cyber ​​Security Center (NCSC) was established

[173] Over 40 public and private organizations collaborate here, and the center is a major boost to our national ability to detect and handle computer attacks

[174] The development of a new alert system to detect digital attacks strengthens our ability to protect digital assets

[175] Since 2013, the police have been strengthened by over 3,100 full-time equivalents as of August 2020, and over 2,000 of these are police full-time equivalents

[176] Investments have been made in three new police helicopters, and the National Police Emergency Response Center, which will be operational, is also being completed

[177] Work has been systematically done to further develop civil-military cooperation and total defense, among other things to meet our obligations as a credible NATO ally

[178] The strengthening of preparedness will continue, both through continued investment in important preparedness resources and through work that provides even more efficient utilization of society's overall resources

[179] St. 5 2020–2021 Social security in an uncertain world 1.2 Prevention becomes more important

[180] In this social security report, attention is particularly focused on prevention

[181] Today's risk picture makes prevention increasingly important

[182] Climate change increases the stress from natural events, and globalization increases the risk of the rapid spread of serious infectious diseases

[183] The security situation has deteriorated, leading to an increased risk of espionage, digital mapping and sabotage, and the spread of disinformation and fake news

[184] Society's increased digitalization gives state and non-state actors new tools and arenas to pursue their strategic interests

[185] The Government is strengthening preventive work through regulatory development, implementation of security measures and through further development of knowledge and expertise

[186] Regulatory developments set the framework for preventive work

[187] The government has invested in regulatory development related to both natural events and intentional actions

[188] A new security law came into force in 2019, strengthening our ability to prevent, detect and counteract intentional actions that could affect values that are important to national security

[189] State planning guidelines for climate adaptation were established in 2018, and provide guidance for municipalities' planning work so that risks resulting from climate change are limited or avoided

[190] Digital security is one of the government's priority areas

[191] The government will establish a law on digital security that implements the EU's NIS Directive and continuously assess how EU legal requirements can and should be incorporated into Norwegian law to ensure digital security

[192] Implementing security measures prevents incidents or reduces the harmful effects of serious unwanted incidents that could affect us

[193] It makes society more resilient

[194] The implementation of the Security Act ensures that a reasonable level of security is established for information systems, objects and infrastructure that are worthy of protection

[195] Efforts to combat floods and landslides have been stepped up, and in the period 2014–2019, approximately NOK 1.7 billion has been spent on flood and landslide protection measures from the NVE budget

[196] It is also important that existing security measures are adapted to the current threat landscape

[197] The government will therefore replace the current shelter scheme with a new scheme for safe places to stay

[198] Developing knowledge and expertise is the foundation for all preventive work

[199] In the face of new risks and threats, the ability to understand them and assess appropriate preventive measures is crucial

[200] The establishment of the NCSC within the National Security Authority (NSA) as a hub for information sharing, expertise exchange and cross-sectoral collaboration strengthens expertise building within digital security

[201] The Arctic maritime competence node, which is under construction, will contribute to responsible, sustainable and efficient shipping in polar waters

[202] The threat of disinformation is being met, among other things, by strengthening the ability to critique sources through the new curriculum for primary and secondary schools, and through preventive measures aimed at influencing elections

[203] Learning from exercises and incidents improves the ability to handle future incidents

[204] Work is continuing to ensure that training needs are identified, and that exercises are planned and anchored with the actors involved

[205] Work on societal security must be adapted to the world we live in, and based on the challenges we face

[206] Changes in the security policy landscape, climate change, globalization, technological development and urbanization Figure

[209] Social security in an uncertain world is of great importance for the work on social security

[210] The same applies to the economic room for maneuver in coming years' budgets, which will also be affected by the corona pandemic

[211] Previous public safety report

[212] St. 10 (2016–

[213] Risk in a safe society, cf. Recommendation

[214] § (2016–2017), emphasized that a 100 percent secure society is neither desirable nor possible

[215] The costs of risk-reducing measures may exceed the benefits, and the measures may conflict with fundamental values such as self-determination, personal freedom, legal certainty and privacy

[216] The work on societal safety is therefore about more than identifying and managing risk

[217] It is also about considering what kind of society we want to develop and live in

[218] The government is working towards a safe society

[219] At the same time, there is a limit to security measures, and risk must be accepted to a certain extent

[220] These assessments from the previous social security report remain valid

[221] The security policy picture is more uncertain than before

[222] We see great powers with increasing global ambitions, and tendencies towards increasing rivalry between them

[223] The distinction between peace, crisis and war is becoming less clear

[224] Some actors are increasingly combining overt and covert military and non-military means

[225] At the same time, we see a tendency for multilateral cooperation to be challenged because large countries choose to solve common problems bilaterally, or in the worst case, unilaterally

[226] This is challenging for Norway because international cooperation is crucial for our security, economy and welfare

[227] The global trading system was already characterized by increasing protectionism before the corona pandemic

[228] There is a risk that the corona crisis will worsen this and lead to increased trade barriers

[229] Climate change is increasing the intensity and frequency of extreme weather events such as heat waves, torrential rain and strong winds

[230] The distinction between climatic seasons becomes less clear, for example, floods may affect more people year-round

[231] Increased mobility of people, ideas, goods, services and capital across national borders has provided the basis for economic growth and increased welfare

[232] As the world has become more interconnected, the threat and vulnerability picture has also changed

[233] The consequences of unwanted incidents spread quickly between countries

[234] The importance of geographical distance decreases as people travel both further and more

[235] The risk of the spread of infectious diseases is increasing, as the coronavirus pandemic fully illustrates (see Chapter

[236] More and more products and services depend on ICT infrastructure and network connectivity

[237] This creates potential vulnerabilities that can be exploited by actors who want to harm us

[238] We trade, communicate and share enormous amounts of information over the internet

[239] The rise of social media and other digital platforms creates new opportunities for influence, including through disinformation

[240] At the same time, developments give us new opportunities to handle the challenges we face

[241] Innovation and technological development, and cooperation across borders, are very important for this work

[242] The breadth of the challenge and tighter financial framework mean that it will increasingly be necessary to assess whether certain risks and threats should be prioritized over others, and which considerations should weigh most heavily when preventive measures are to be implemented and preparedness is to be dimensioned

[243] For example, we must consider to what extent civil preparedness should be dimensioned for situations high on the crisis spectrum (for example, armed conflict) or whether it should primarily be dimensioned for situations lower on the crisis spectrum (floods, accidents, etc.), where we base our approach on being able to scale up preparedness when needed

[244] In other words, the work on social security faces demanding prioritization decisions

[245] The report does not provide answers to these questions, but the government wants to contribute to transparency and awareness of them, and to lay the foundation for good discussions

[246] The prioritization challenges are discussed in more detail in Chapter

[247] The coronavirus pandemic The outbreak of the coronavirus, which has been named SARS-CoV-2, began in China and quickly spread to several other countries

[248] At the end of February, the first case of coronavirus was registered in Norway

[249] On March 11, 2020, the World Health Organization declared the outbreak a pandemic

[250] On March 12, the health authorities, with the support of the Minister of Health and Social Care and the Prime Minister, therefore decided to implement drastic measures to combat the spread of the infection

[251] The pandemic and the infection control measures that were implemented have had major consequences for all parts of society

[252] It is during crises that we test our preparedness and systems

[253] Handling the pandemic is a test of how well prepared we are and how established systems function under stress

[254] The handling has followed the general emergency preparedness principles

[255] St. 5 2020–2021 Social security in an uncertain world the principles of responsibility, proximity, equality and cooperation (see chapter

[256] The crisis has been handled in accordance with established principles, plans, and routines for handling incidents

[257] At the same time, the incident affects many aspects of public safety work, such as digital security, security of supply and work against infectious diseases (see Chapter

[258] The pandemic emphasizes the importance of continuously working to further develop our ability to handle unwanted incidents and to maintain continuity in critical societal functions

[259] At the same time, work on public safety also includes areas that are not as affected by the pandemic, such as rescue services, preparedness against natural events, and security of supply for power and water

[260] It is important that systematic work is done to further develop these parts of societal security, even though we are in a very demanding situation with the pandemic

[261] This White Paper was originally planned to be presented to the Storting in April

[262] However, due to the outbreak of coronavirus, work on the report was put on hold

[263] A preliminary discussion of the handling of the corona pandemic is included in chapter

[264] The message does not contain an evaluation of the government's handling of the pandemic so far

[265] Reference is made here to that evaluation

[267] The administrative system for crisis management at the ministry level

[268] The government has the ultimate responsibility for preparedness in Norway

[269] At the ministry level, the administrative apparatus for central crisis management is based on three main elements: – The ministry responsible for a sector is also responsible for emergency planning and measures in a crisis situation (cf. the principle of responsibility

[270] The lead ministry is responsible for coordinating the handling of a crisis at the ministry level

[271] The Crisis Council is the highest administrative co-ordinating body at ministry level

[272] Crisis Support Unit (KSE

[273] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security shall, if necessary, provide support to the Crisis Council in their crisis management

[274] After the terrorist attack on July 22, 2011, it was decided that the Ministry of Justice and Public Security will be the permanent lead ministry in civil national crises unless otherwise decided

[275] When it comes to crises and incidents that affect one sector to a significantly greater extent than others, it may be appropriate to assign lead ministry responsibility to the ministry that is most affected

[276] During the corona pandemic, the Ministry of Justice and Public Security has been the lead ministry, with the exception of a short period in March, see chapter

[277] The system for central crisis management in Norway is described in more detail in Appendix II

[278] Following the terrorist attacks on July 22, 2011, a number of measures have been implemented to improve preparedness

[279] Much has been done to ensure that the resources that did not find each other in 2011 will now find each other and cooperate well in the event of major and unexpected events

[280] The police's cooperation with other emergency services and the Armed Forces has been expanded and strengthened, and the requirements to follow up on findings from incidents and exercises have been tightened for the civilian side of the state administration (see also section

[281] Several joint centers have been established in important areas to ensure good coordination

[282] These are measures that directly strengthen our ability to recognize risks, implement and collaborate

[286] Public safety, state security and national security

[287] The government has the ultimate responsibility for safeguarding public safety, state security and national security

[288] Societal security is about society's ability to protect itself against and handle events that threaten fundamental values ​​and functions and put life and health at risk

[289] Such events can be triggered by nature, be the result of technical or human errors or deliberate actions

[290] The work includes preparedness against natural events such as floods and landslides, accidents such as fires and shipwrecks, and intentional acts such as digital attacks and terrorist acts

[291] The purpose of state security is to safeguard the state's existence, sovereignty, and territorial integrity, and the Storting has been briefed on, and has discussed, the follow-up to the terrorist acts of 22 July 2011 on several occasions

[302] St. 5 Social security in an uncertain world political freedom of action

[303] Norwegian security and defense policy is intended to ensure national security

[304] State security has traditionally been linked to the defense of the territory against armed attacks, but it can also be challenged through influence with various other forms of pressure against Norwegian authorities and societal actors

[305] When state security is threatened, it can legitimize the use of the full range of state instruments, such as diplomatic, international law and economic instruments, international dialogue and cooperation, as well as the use of military force

[306] In a situation where state security is threatened, civilian authorities have the task of both protecting civil society and supporting the military efforts of the Armed Forces

[307] Social security is also important for safeguarding state security

[308] Social security and state security are mutually dependent on each other

[309] Certain civilian goods and services such as fuel supply and access to transport infrastructure may be critical for safeguarding societal security, but also crucial for the Armed Forces in safeguarding national security

[310] At the same time, civilian actors may be dependent on assistance from the Armed Forces in critical situations, for example in connection with transport needs when handling an incident

[311] Social developments and changes in the threat landscape are increasing the dependencies between civilian and military sides

[312] The emergence of new security challenges, including threats from non-state actors, can challenge both societal security and national security

[313] Never before has technology that can threaten state security been available to so many

[314] Compound threats, where different instruments are used to support and reinforce each other (see Chapter 9), can make it more difficult to identify security-threatening activities, understand the overall threat picture and which actors are behind them

[315] The distinction between societal security and state security is becoming more blurred, and it may become Box 1.1 Key concepts in the report Emergency preparedness is planned and prepared measures that enable us to handle undesirable events so that the consequences are as small as possible

[316] Prevention is establishing measures in advance of events to reduce the likelihood or consequences of an unwanted event

[317] Fundamental national functions are services, production and other forms of activity that are of such importance that a complete or partial loss of the function would have consequences for the state's ability to safeguard national security interests

[318] Crisis is defined as an undesirable situation with a high degree of uncertainty and potentially unacceptable consequences for the individuals, organizations or states affected

[319] National security is defined as the area of state security and a limited part of the area of societal security that is of significant importance to the state's ability to safeguard national security interests

[320] The national security interests are stated in Section 1-5 of the Security Act

[321] Risk is an expression of the combination of the probability and consequences of an undesirable event

[322] Societal security is about society's ability to protect itself against and handle events that threaten fundamental values ​​and functions and put life and health at risk

[323] Such events can be triggered by nature, be the result of technical or human errors or deliberate actions

[324] Critical societal functions are those functions that are necessary to safeguard the basic needs of the population and society and the population's sense of security

[325] Basic needs are defined as “food, water, heat, security and the like.”

[326] The facilities and systems that are necessary to maintain society's critical functions are referred to as critical infrastructure

[327] State security is about safeguarding the state's existence, sovereignty, territorial integrity and political freedom of action

[328] Vulnerability is an expression of a system's inability to resist an unwanted action or event, as well as its inability to resume its function

[329] The Total Defence Concept is about mutual support and cooperation between the Armed Forces and civil society in connection with prevention, emergency planning, crisis management and consequence management across the entire crisis spectrum from peace via security policy crises to armed conflict

[330] Threat is the capacity and intention of an actor or several actors (state, group, individual) to carry out intentional, unwanted actions

[331] St. 5 2020–2021 Societal security in an uncertain world more challenging to see who is actually affected by a particular threat

[332] The concept of national security is linked to the Security Act and concerns safeguarding national security interests, which in the law are understood as the country's sovereignty, territorial integrity and democratic form of government, as well as overarching security policy interests related to a) the activities, security and freedom of action of the highest state bodies, b) defence, security and preparedness, c) relations with other states and international organisations, d) economic stability and freedom of action and e) the basic functionality of society and the basic security of the population

[333] The scope of the Security Act is the area of state security and that part of the area of societal security that is of significant importance to the state's ability to safeguard national security interests

[334] The new Security Act has a somewhat broader scope than the act it replaced

[335] The new area of ​​activity is adapted to societal developments and a changed threat landscape, including the close link between societal security and state security

[336] The scope of the Act is further defined through the identification of fundamental national functions

[337] These are services, production or other forms of activity that are of such importance that the complete or partial loss of the function would have consequences for the state's ability to safeguard national security interests (see further discussion in Chapter

[338] This message deals with societal security and preventive national security

[345] UN Sustainable Development Goals In 2015, the UN's 193 member states agreed on 17 common goals for sustainable development as part of the Agenda

[346] The sustainability goals are interdependent

[347] For example, war, conflict and security are closely linked to social and economic development

[348] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security is responsible for coordinating the work on Goal 16 Peace and Justice

[349] Norway is perceived as a safe country to live in, and has a well-functioning legal system with well-developed and well-functioning institutions

[350] World Justice Project

[351] s Rule of Law Index, which measures how the judiciary and authorities are perceived, ranked Norway as the second best country in 2019, after Denmark

[352] Several of the sustainability goals are important for societal security

[353] Combating climate change, building robust infrastructure, and promoting good health and peaceful and inclusive societies are some examples

[354] The follow-up of the Sustainable Development Goals can help reduce the risk of conflict and instability abroad, and thus improve the basis for societal security

[361] Structure and delimitation

[362] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security shall regularly prepare reports to the Storting that set out overall goals and measures and summarize the status and results within the field of public security

[363] Reports to the Storting in the field of social security are part of the national planning basis for social security work

[364] Based on the challenge picture, the government will in this report particularly promote measures within the following seven areas: The Covid-19 pandemic, Civil-military cooperation and total defence, Preventive national security, Digital security, Composite threats, Prevention and preparedness locally and regionally, Prevention, preparedness and rescue services in our northern sea areas

[365] These seven themes are discussed in their own chapters

[366] In addition, the report contains separate chapters on research and development, on international cooperation, and on ongoing and completed measures that the government has implemented that have strengthened work on societal security

[367] The four chapters on civil-military cooperation and total defence (Chapter 6), preventive national security (Chapter 7), digital security (Chapter 8) and complex threats (Chapter 9) are partly closely interrelated

[368] The use of digital tools can constitute a significant part of complex threats, and work on national security encompasses both issues related to digital security and complex threats

[369] In addition, all three of these topics are central to civil-military cooperation and important in total defense

[370] Cross-references have been included in the various chapters to show key points of connection between them

[428] The report presents the government's policy for work on social security in Norway in a four-year perspective

[431] The chapter describes how work on societal security is affected by, among other things, changes in the security policy landscape, globalization, digitalization, urbanization and climate change

[432] Prevention and prioritization considerations

[433] It is neither desirable nor possible to create a risk-free society

[434] The work on societal security therefore includes deciding what constitutes acceptable risk

[435] To clarify that assessments of risk acceptance are part of the responsibility principle, the government will clarify that the responsibility principle implies that the responsible body takes a position on what constitutes acceptable risk

[436] The principles of responsibility, equality, proximity, and cooperation are fundamental to the work on societal security

[437] – Further develop society's resilience through increased emphasis on preventive work

[438] – Clarifying the responsibility principle to make it clear that assessments of risk acceptance are part of the exercise of the responsibility principle

[439] The Covid-19 pandemic is the most serious crisis Norway has experienced since World War II

[440] The pandemic has major consequences for all parts of society, both in terms of health loss, consequences for vulnerable children and young people, and economic and other social harms

[441] The pandemic is also a significant risk to public safety

[442] – Continue to manage the pandemic so that the disease burden in Norway is low and the health and care services have the capacity to handle the influx of patients

[443] – Continue efforts to get the population to follow basic infection control measures

[444] – Strengthen efforts with testing, isolation, infection tracing and quarantine to detect and control local outbreaks early

[445] – Ensure that the relaxation of infection control measures takes place in a controlled, gradual manner and over time

[446] Consideration for children and young people is prioritized first, followed by consideration for jobs and business

[447] – Continue cooperation with the EU to secure vaccines for the population of Norway and contribute to the international effort to ensure all countries have access to vaccines against COVID-19. – Continue efforts to build up emergency preparedness capacities for protective equipment, medical equipment and pharmaceuticals in the health and care services. – Continuously develop the knowledge base so that measures are effective in handling the pandemic with the least possible negative consequences for the individual citizen and for society

[448] Measures must be useful and proportionate, and the socio-economic effects of measures must be emphasized as far as possible

[449] – Continue to monitor the economic situation closely and, if necessary, consider measures to support Norwegian businesses and Norwegian workers who have been or are affected by the corona pandemic

[450] – Facilitate relevant documentation and otherwise assist the Corona Commission in their work

[451] – Conduct self-evaluations in the ministries, cf. requirements in the social security instructions, and ensure learning in the ministries and in public agencies

[552] Social security in an uncertain world The challenge

[553] This chapter explains key factors that influence the challenge picture

[554] Targeted and effective work on societal security and national security requires knowledge of the challenges and trends that can affect security

[555] Security policy developments Norway's security depends on a rules-based international order and binding multilateral cooperation, as highlighted in Report

[556] Norway's role and interests in multilateral cooperation

[557] S (2019–

[558] The foundation of Norway's security is international law and our membership in the United Nations (UN) and the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), in addition to close regional and bilateral security policy cooperation with close allies, particularly the United States

[559] The security policy situation for Norway is changing

[560] One of the reasons is that the rules-based world order is increasingly being challenged by countries with different value sets

[561] It is expected that increased rivalry between the world's great powers will shape developments in the years ahead

[562] Security policy developments are also influenced by societal and technological developments

[563] The increased digitalization of society gives state and non-state actors new tools and arenas to pursue their strategic interests

[564] The use of a combination of overt and covert military and non-military instruments, so called mixed use of instruments, challenges the distinction between peace, security-political crisis and armed conflict

[565] These are situations where an actor uses a range of different instruments to influence actors in Norway

[566] Disinformation, investments in business, influence through diplomacy, recruitment or placement of unfaithful servants in commercial and public enterprises, and digital attacks are some examples

[567] The agents can be used separately or combined and coordinated so that they support and reinforce each other (see Chapter

[568] Over the past decade, Russia has carried out a comprehensive modernization of its armed forces, and the development is planned to continue in the coming years

[569] Russia has clearly demonstrated its willingness to use military force to achieve political goals in Georgia, Ukraine and Syria, as well as an increased use of several instruments to weaken cohesion in and between Western countries

[570] In the Norwegian context, the negative development can be illustrated by Russian military exercises of attack profiles against Norwegian targets and interference with GPS signals in Finnmark

[571] One of the most important trends in the geopolitical landscape of our time is China's growth

[572] Economic growth is followed by clear political, technological, cultural and military ambitions

[573] China is emerging as a global superpower, increasingly defining and influencing the international agenda

[574] China's military forces are being heavily modernised

[575] Both the Norwegian Intelligence Service and the Police Security Service (PST) name China as a challenge for Norway as well

[576] North Africa and the Middle East are areas characterized by wars, conflicts and crises, destabilization and unpredictability

[577] If young people in these areas do not receive better opportunities than today, the basis for migration and violent extremism could become even greater

[587] Climate change is one of the greatest challenges of our time

[588] According to the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, increasing emissions of CO2 and other greenhouse gases from, among other things, power generation, industry, agriculture, cars and aircraft have contributed to the atmospheric CO2 content being

[589] Social security in an uncertain world higher than at any time in the last 800,000 years

[590] Increased concentrations of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere enhance the greenhouse effect

[591] The world is getting warmer and the risk of unforeseen changes in the climate system with serious consequences is increasing

[592] The direct effects of climate change are linked to increased intensity and frequency of extreme weather such as heat waves, torrential rain and strong winds

[593] Changes in weather and nature intensify stresses from natural events such as landslides and floods

[594] In addition, the ocean, access to arable land and other natural resources are changing

[595] Climate change can also contribute to the increased spread of diseases

[596] The changes will thus have negative consequences for both economic activity and living conditions

[597] The consequences of climate change are greatest for vulnerable developing countries that have limited capacity to handle the stresses

[598] In these countries, climate change could become a source of conflict and unrest, for example by reducing access to food and water

[599] The development could also lead to increased migration pressure, partly because land areas become uninhabitable

[600] The indirect consequences can thus be large, even for richer countries

[601] Climate change also has consequences for Norway

[602] According to the Norwegian Meteorological Institute, we can expect an increase in temperature and precipitation throughout the country and throughout all seasons

[603] Natural events are already a significant part of the challenges in Norway

[604] Going forward, we must expect more extreme weather and increased stress from natural events

[605] The risk of flooding, landslides, storm surges and stormwater is increasing

[606] More extreme precipitation, such as torrential rain, means that landslides may occur in areas that have until now been protected from this

[607] We are regularly exposed to natural events such as landslides and floods

[628] Norway has benefited greatly from globalization

[629] Our prosperity is largely based on international trade and investment across borders

[630] As the world has become more interconnected, the threat and vulnerability picture has also changed

[631] We depend on the functioning of the world market for important commodities

[632] Dependence on long supply lines and reduction in inventory increases vulnerability to production and logistics failures

[633] At the same time, the importance of geographical distance is reduced when people travel both further and more

[655] International trade and cooperation arrangements can be exploited for hostile purposes International trade and cooperation across borders is a source of economic growth, technological advances and increased welfare

[656] However, this openness can become a vulnerability if it is abused

[657] For example, cross-border investments can be exploited by unauthorized parties as a covert means to gain insight into sensitive and strategic information

[660] Risks related to failures in value chains for critical goods and services

[661] Norway has an open economy where imports are at least as important as market access for our exports

[662] This means that we are largely dependent on importing goods and services that are critical for the population and for businesses

[663] Internationally, the production of goods is largely organized in so-called global value and supply chains, where different parts of a good are produced in different places in the world, depending on price and access to materials, labor and expertise

[664] Norwegian data flows largely through foreign-controlled networks, and a significant part of our critical infrastructure has components that are manufactured by foreign companies abroad

[665] Such specialization and geographical division of labor provides economic benefits

[666] However, long supply lines can be confusing and a source of vulnerability, as failure in one part of the chain can disrupt both production and logistics

[667] Limited stockpiling of critical goods and services further increases this vulnerability

[668] These challenges have been highlighted during the coronavirus pandemic

[669] As the pandemic spread around the world, there was a sharp increase in global demand for respirators, testing equipment, and infection control equipment such as face masks, gloves, protective suits, and eye protection

[670] These products are mainly produced in other countries, with China as a key player

[671] At the same time, global transport capacity was reduced as a result of the pandemic

[672] In sum, this meant that the acquisition of necessary equipment and the building up of warehouses became very demanding (see also Chapter

[675] Economic inequality in a country can have a negative impact on both interpersonal trust and trust in the authorities

[681] Risk analysis of drug shortages

[682] In recent years, the issue of drug shortages has become increasingly relevant

[683] This is a global challenge

[684] The most important reasons for shortages are production problems, withdrawal of drugs from the market, logistics problems and rapid increases in demand

[685] International cooperation is important to reduce the number of serious shortage situations and ensure good information

[686] Norway participates in cooperation at the Nordic, European and global levels

[687] The Directorate for Civil Protection and Emergency Preparedness (DSB) conducted a risk analysis of drug shortages in Norway in 2018, in close collaboration with the health sector

[688] In continuation of DSB's report, the Directorate of Health has reviewed the drug preparedness and proposed a number of measures, reports IS-2837 and IS-2873 delivered in June 2019 and February 2019, respectively

[689] The reports are being followed up by the Ministry of Health and Care Services, and proposals for legislative amendments to strengthen the Norwegian Medicines Agency's authority have been put to consultation, among other things

[690] In connection with the corona pandemic, temporary regulations allow for a ban on parallel exports, a reporting obligation, prioritization and rationing, and emergency stocks of critical pharmaceuticals are being built up at the national level

[691] Social security in an uncertain world Increasing inequality in society can reduce social cohesion, create perceptions of injustice, and intensify contradictions between groups in society

[692] A more polarized society can make the population more vulnerable to actors who spread false information

[693] Polarized societies are more vulnerable to disinformation campaigns, which seek to fuel differences to increase division and undermine democratic processes

[694] Norway is among the countries with the lowest inequality, both when we look at the distribution of income and with regard to broader indicators of the distribution of living conditions and quality of life

[695] Norwegian society is also characterized by a high level of trust

[696] The citizens of Norway have a high degree of trust in both the authorities and each other

[697] Trust promotes cohesion, cooperation and participation in society's various arenas, and facilitates the effective functioning of markets, democracy and the rule of law

[698] The high level of trust in Norway makes society more robust

[699] At the same time, trust can vary between groups in society and contribute to polarization between groups with different degrees of trust in the authorities and others

[700] People with low education and low incomes generally have lower trust in governing institutions than those with higher education and higher income levels

[701] The Government's efforts to contribute to social sustainability and counteract inequality and the consequences of inequality are discussed in more detail in report

[703] Increased risk of rapid spread of serious infectious diseases

[704] Infectious diseases pose a significant threat

[705] Globalization, population growth, urbanization, climate change and increased travel activity contribute to outbreaks occurring more frequently than before and to their ability to spread rapidly over large distances

[707] In addition, in recent years we have had several international outbreaks of diseases such as Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS), Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS), pandemic influenza, Ebola virus disease and Zika virus fever, all of which have required major preparedness efforts

[724] Social security in an uncertain world mobile networks (5G), the use of sensor technology and artificial intelligence, we will have new digital services that will renew and improve the way we live and work

[725] Our everyday lives are digital, primarily for the good of individuals, businesses and the public administration

[726] At the same time, digitalization is changing the risk picture

[727] According to the National Security Authority (NSM), increasing complexity in digital systems and value chains is an important reason for increasing vulnerabilities

[728] Digital ecosystems consist of multiple computers, multiple systems, multiple protocols, multiple services, and multiple and longer value chains

[729] All these digital solutions are interconnected and create confusing dependencies

[730] The digital space provides threat actors with opportunities to commit data breaches, engage in espionage, carry out digital attacks and conduct influence campaigns

[731] There has been an increase in targeted data breaches against Norwegian authorities and businesses

[732] Particularly vulnerable targets are enterprises within Norwegian state administration, enterprises that support critical infrastructure and Norwegian technology companies that are world leaders in their segment

[733] ICT crime is increasing as actors increasingly use digital tools to illegally acquire assets

[734] Actors behind digital attacks usually exploit the weakest link in a value chain and look for the easiest path to the target

[735] The perpetrators are often organized, have high technological knowledge and can be located anywhere in the world

[736] The rapid development makes it challenging to predict which threats and vulnerabilities will characterize the risk picture

[737] Ransomware, industrial espionage, and foreign intelligence activity will likely continue to shape the risk landscape going forward

[738] In addition, a large proportion of adverse events are unintentional

[739] Failures or outages in digital systems and services occur due to human error, software errors, equipment failures, natural events, or a combination of these

[740] Urbanization in Norway

[741] Urbanization means that people, markets and activities move from rural to urban areas

[742] It is a worldwide trend that has been going on for a long time

[743] Today, about 80 percent of the population in Norway lives in urban areas, and there is a clear tendency for the most central parts of the country to also have the highest population growth

[744] Greater educational opportunities and career opportunities are key reasons why people move from rural areas to cities

[745] Urbanization is leading to population growth in central areas, while the rural areas are experiencing emigration

[749] Municipalities with sufficient capacity and expertise are important for public safety

[750] Emigration from rural municipalities also reduces the recruitment base for voluntary organizations in the rescue service

[751] In areas close to the city center, increased density and more paved surfaces can put pressure on green areas in cities and towns

[763] The challenges create a need for coordination The challenges are cross-border, cross-sectoral and affect authorities and private actors at central, regional and local levels

[764] The system is therefore necessary to: – ensure uniform and harmonized social security work across sectors – avoid gray areas and clarify the division of responsibility for overlapping areas – ensure coherent and integrated measures and instruments – be able to set cross-sectoral priorities at the national level – handle interdependencies, including dependencies between critical societal functions – ensure effective utilization of society’s collective resources – support effective crisis management

[766] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security also has a central role in international cooperation, which is an important part of societal security work

[779] Societal security in an uncertain world Prevention and prioritization

[780] The challenge picture sets guidelines for work on societal security

[781] We must continuously develop our ability to prevent, handle and follow up on unwanted incidents

[782] At the same time, tighter economic frameworks place increased demands on prioritization and efficient resource utilization

[783] This has two important consequences for the work on social security

[784] The preventive part of the work will become more important, and there will be demanding trade-offs and prioritizations between different considerations

[785] Several of the principles and assessments presented in sections 4.2–4.4 are made more relevant by the coronavirus pandemic

[786] However, this report does not contain an assessment of the extent to which the authorities have been able to handle the pandemic in line with these

[787] This will be relevant to return to after the Corona Commission has submitted its report

[788] Government policy

[789] It is neither desirable nor possible to create a risk-free society

[790] The work on societal security therefore includes deciding what constitutes acceptable risk

[791] To clarify that assessments of risk acceptance are part of the responsibility principle, the government will clarify that the responsibility principle implies that the responsible body takes a position on what constitutes acceptable risk

[792] The principles of responsibility, equality, proximity, and cooperation are fundamental to the work on societal security

[793] – Further develop society's resilience through increased emphasis on preventive work

[794] – Clarifying the responsibility principle to make it clear that assessments of risk acceptance are part of the exercise of the responsibility principle

[795] Prevention is becoming more important Prevention involves taking measures to reduce the possibility of an unwanted event, or to reduce the consequences of a possible event in advance

[796] By preventing, we can protect life and health, economic, material and environmental values, and we can ensure continuity in important societal functions

[797] The breadth and complexity of the risk picture requires a broad spectrum of preventive measures, and preventive work involves a number of actors

[798] Central categories of instruments are regulation (legal provisions, routines, etc.), technological solutions, physical and digital security measures and awareness-raising work

[799] The measures can be aimed at individuals (for example, training and sanctions that reduce risk behavior), non-profit and voluntary organizations (for example, in the work against radicalization), and at business and government actors (for example, avoiding the construction of housing and infrastructure in areas particularly prone to landslides

[800] Table 4.1 shows examples of prevention measures for various undesirable incidents

[801] Prevention is knowledge-based work. Prevention involves using knowledge about cause-and-effect relationships to reduce risk, that is, how different vulnerabilities and risks can lead to different types of undesirable incidents

[802] For some incidents, we have good knowledge of cause-and-effect relationships

[803] One example is injuries and accidents related to the use of electricity

[804] We have good knowledge about vulnerabilities and how electrical power can be used safely and securely

[805] This knowledge forms the basis for the design of regulations and routines that prevent unwanted incidents caused by electricity

[806] For other incidents, for example related to digital security and intentional unwanted actions, the cause-effect relationships may be more complex

[807] Precise and effective prevention measures are based on a good knowledge base

[826] Societal security in an uncertain world The security instruction requires that ministries have an overview of risks and vulnerabilities for their sector

[827] Key sources of knowledge include overall national planning bases such as crisis scenarios, overviews of critical societal functions and other strategic documents on risk, threats and vulnerability, for example assessments from the Police Security Service (PST), the Intelligence Service (E-tjenesten), the National Security Authority (NSM) and others

[828] Other central sources of knowledge are research and evaluations

[829] For some unwanted incidents, certain actors have a particularly important role in preventive work

[830] This applies, for example, to the prevention of damage from landslides and floods, where the most effective way is to avoid building housing and infrastructure in particularly vulnerable areas

[831] With regard to the prevention of damage from landslides and floods, the municipality, as the planning authority, is a key player (see Chapter

[832] When it comes to infrastructure, owners, such as the Norwegian Public Roads Administration, county municipalities and Bane Nor, have a responsibility to map hazards and take measures to reduce the risk of damage as a result of natural hazards

[833] Prevention is often economically profitable. The costs of prevention can be significantly lower than the costs of handling incidents and repairing damage

[834] Once the incident has occurred, both the acute handling and the follow-up work can require significant resources

[835] Undesirable events can result in extensive costs related to life and health, the environment, and material assets

[836] Flood and landslide protection are examples of measures that provide great socio-economic benefits in relation to the costs of the measures

[837] Assessments of socio-economic benefits in relation to costs form the basis for the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate's (NVE) assistance for flood and landslide protection measures

[838] In light of the economic perspectives outlined in Report

[840] S (2016–2017), preventive work will become even more important in the coming years

[841] Similarly, a digital attack can have major consequences for the daily operations of affected businesses, and require large resources to handle the attack and restore necessary functions

[842] On March 19, 2019, the company Norsk Hydro was hit by a comprehensive digital attack

[843] The consequences affected Hydro's entire global organization, and in the fall of 2019 the company estimated the total cost at around NOK 550-650 million

[844] It is important that businesses that are exposed to digital attacks notify and report the situation

[845] Sharing knowledge strengthens our ability to prevent, detect, warn and manage digital incidents

[846] Prevention creates more resilient societies Preventive work makes us reflect on vulnerabilities, risks and possible measures, and therefore contributes to increased awareness of various aspects of the work on societal security and national security

[847] Prevention must take place in both the private and public sectors and at all levels of government

[848] The individual citizen must also be given sufficient knowledge and awareness of how values can be secured

[849] Prevention must be prioritized in general social planning, whether it concerns the choice of road routes, the location and security of important buildings, who is given access to sensitive information, the choice of technological solutions within the cyber domain, or the selection of security measures

[865] Prioritization considerations in work on societal security

[866] This is the government's second report on social security to the Storting

[867] In the previous report to the Storting, Report

[868] St. 10 (2016–

[869] Risk in a safe society, cf. Recommendation

[870] S (2016–2017), the government described key challenges and prerequisites for living with risk

[871] In the report, the government emphasized that a 100 percent safe society is neither desirable nor possible, that we must always live with a certain risk, and that Norway is a resilient society – rich in human, economic and material resources

[872] Resilience provides good conditions for living with risk

[873] The work on societal security builds on these perspectives from the previous report to the Storting

[874] Parliament 29 (2016–

[875] Perspective report

[876] § 358 (2016–2017), emphasizes that the financial framework will become tighter in the coming years

[877] Over the past 10–15 years, proposals for new plans and measures have been processed with the expectation of increased room for manoeuvre in the budgets

[878] Going forward, it will be increasingly necessary to find funding for new initiatives through reprioritization and cuts

[879] This places increased demands on cost-benefit assessments of measures

[880] The need for prioritization also applies to social security work

[881] Balancing cost against benefit can be demanding

[882] The benefits may be difficult to determine, and there may be uncertainty related to future developments and the effects of the measures

[883] Measures may also conflict with fundamental values such as self-determination, personal freedom, legal certainty and privacy

[884] Some threats and risks may, however, be so serious that they are subject to stricter risk reduction requirements

[885] For example, there are some values ​​in society that are of such importance that the businesses that dispose of them are subject to the Security Act with associated requirements for how they must achieve adequate security

[886] A fundamental trade-off in the work on societal security is to what extent we should prioritize events with low probability and high consequence, or events with high probability and relatively lower consequence

[887] Such assessments may also involve weighing one type of consequence, for example the consequences of an event for critical infrastructure, against other types of consequences, such as the consequences of another event for nature and the environment

[888] It will rarely or never be appropriate to completely eliminate a type of incident from priority, but the probability and possible consequences of incidents will be important factors in prioritizing

[889] A related question is to what extent civil preparedness should be dimensioned for situations high on the crisis spectrum (for example, armed conflict) or whether it should primarily be dimensioned for situations lower on the crisis spectrum (floods, accidents, etc.), where we base our approach on being able to scale up preparedness when needed

[890] If civilian sectors design for worst-case scenarios high on the crisis spectrum, we risk tying up resources that have no application in other situations

[891] On the other hand, it is important that civilian sectors have the capacity to assist the Armed Forces also in situations higher on the crisis spectrum

[892] To a certain extent, this can be achieved by strictly prioritizing civilian resources against the needs of the Armed Forces, but if the civilian resources are dimensioned for incidents lower on the crisis spectrum, there is a risk that they cannot provide the Armed Forces with the support that is desired

[893] In light of the tighter financial framework and the demanding challenges, this type of prioritization discussion will become increasingly important

[894] Other important considerations relate to how preparedness for different types of incidents, geographical areas, or objects should be weighted in relation to each other

[895] For certain risks, it will be appropriate to prioritize densely populated areas, for other risks to prioritize buildings with particular symbolic value, and for still other risks to prioritize areas of particular importance for the defense of the country in a security crisis or military conflict

[896] Risk and vulnerability assessments must form the basis for prioritizing preparedness

[897] The prioritization challenges affect authorities at central, regional and local levels

[898] The outcome of the priorities could affect civil-military cooperation, and their assessments therefore require close cooperation between the civilian and military sides

[899] Social security in an uncertain world The priorities will also be able to influence public-private collaboration (see box 4.2), and close dialogue with the private sector is therefore important

[900] Many of the challenges within the field of societal security cut across sector boundaries

[901] For example, digital incidents can affect businesses and services in all sectors

[902] Natural events such as forest fires, storms and floods can have an impact on the health sector, fire services and the police, and often require assistance from the Armed Forces

[903] The ability to set cross-sectoral priorities at the national level will therefore become even more important in the years ahead, both between civilian sectors and between the civilian side and the Armed Forces

[904] Risk acceptance – clarification of the responsibility principle

[905] It is neither desirable nor possible to create a risk-free society

[906] The work on societal security therefore includes deciding what constitutes acceptable risk

[907] The work on societal security is based on the four principles: the principle of responsibility, the principle of equality, the principle of proximity and the principle of cooperation (see box

[908] The principle of responsibility means that the organization that is responsible for a subject area in a normal situation is also responsible for the necessary emergency preparedness preparations and for handling extraordinary incidents in the area

[909] There is, however, a limit to how far one can go to reduce risk, and assessment of acceptable risk must therefore be included in the work

[910] In these assessments, it is often necessary to consider what options for risk reduction exist, including which measures are justifiable based on cost-benefit assessments

[911] The assessments must also consider any negative consequences for fundamental values such as self-determination, personal freedom and privacy

[912] To clarify that assessments of risk acceptance are part of the responsibility principle, the government will clarify the responsibility principle with the following addition in italicized text

[913] Box 4.2 Social security depends on good public-private cooperation Public-private cooperation refers here to all types of arrangements in which the public sector interacts with the private sector to solve tasks in the area of social security

[914] Several private actors have a significant responsibility for societal security, for example by managing critical infrastructure

[915] Private actors also have an important role in security of supply, including power supply, e-communications, food supply, fuel supply, pharmaceutical supply and transport

[916] Various schemes for public-private collaboration are therefore important

[917] Among the established schemes for public-private cooperation in Norway, the following can be mentioned

[918] The notification system for digital infrastructure (VDI

[919] The National Security Authority organizes and operates a set of capabilities to detect and verify attempted digital attacks against Norwegian infrastructure

[920] Public and private organizations can request to join VDI and deploy these capabilities in their infrastructure

[921] – The Ekom Security Forum is a forum for the exchange of information between authorities and private players within ekom

[922] – The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries has a formal collaboration with the shipping industry through the NORTRASHIP management and through an agreement on shipping preparedness with the Norwegian Shipowners' Association

[923] — The Food Emergency Preparedness Council, the Fuel Emergency Preparedness Council and the Building and Construction Emergency Preparedness Council are advisory bodies

[924] for the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries in emergency planning and in crises

[925] The councils consist of representatives from the largest food distributors, key fuel players, and nationwide contractors and industry organizations within construction and construction preparedness

[926] – The Safety Forum is a forum with representatives from the authorities and the parties in the working life within the Norwegian petroleum industry, which aims to promote cooperation and knowledge development on, among other things, safety issues

[927] – The Armed Forces' agreements with private actors

[929] Social security in an uncertain world

[930] The responsibility principle means that the organization that is responsible for a subject area in a normal situation is also responsible for necessary emergency preparedness preparations and for handling extraordinary incidents in the area

[931] The responsible body must decide what is an acceptable risk

[932] Assessment of acceptable risk is included in any assessment of opportunities for risk reduction and assessment of appropriate mitigation measures

[933] For example, if a certain set of security measures are implemented around and in a building, we accept the risks that the security measures will not work against

[934] It is important that responsible authorities are aware of this, and the clarification of the principle of responsibility should contribute to this

[935] If necessary, acceptable risk must be clarified with the superior authority

[936] Input from relevant actors can be useful support for the responsible body's decision on risk acceptance, and thus for upholding the principle of responsibility and the principle of cooperation

[937] It is often easier to decide what is acceptable risk for limited functions and tasks

[938] For example, it may be easier to assess risk associated with individual physical objects than it is for securing functions that are supported by a number of underlying input factors and services

[939] Critical societal functions and fundamental national functions have also become increasingly dependent on long and confusing digital value chains, which often span many sectors and several countries

[940] The clarification of the principle could nevertheless contribute to increased awareness of roles, responsibilities and risks

[941] The fact that a sector authority accepts a certain risk within an area does not mean that the authority can waive its responsibility

[942] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security's coordination role is to ensure comprehensive and coordinated preparedness nationally, across all civilian sectors and critical societal functions

[943] The Ministry, through its coordination role (see section 3.6 and Appendix 1), has a responsibility to ensure that the ministries carry out risk assessments

[944] Supervision of the ministries' social security work and preventive security work (see section 12.4) are important instruments in this respect

[945] The coordination role also requires the Ministry of Justice and Public Security to have an overview of the state of affairs in the area of public security and ensure that any issues across sectors are handled

[946] This also applies to any questions related to risk acceptance

[947] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security also has overall responsibility for coordinating preventive security work in the civilian sector

[948] The Ministry of Defense has similar responsibilities in the defense sector

[949] Clarifying the principle of responsibility can contribute to increased awareness of remaining risks

[950] For example, there is a limit to how far rescue helicopters can fly over the ocean before they have to return to base

[951] Knowledge of this limit can be important for a skipper's choice of sailing route

[952] Communicating the scope of risk-reducing measures and remaining risks to relevant actors can provide a basis for implementing internal preparedness measures

[953] The four basic principles for working with societal security

[954] • The responsibility principle means that the organization that is responsible for a subject area in a normal situation is also responsible for necessary emergency preparedness preparations and for handling extraordinary incidents in the area

[955] The responsible body must decide what is acceptable risk

[956] • The principle of similarity means that the organization one operates with during crises should initially be as similar as possible to the organization one has on a daily basis

[957] • The principle of subsidiarity means that crises should be handled organizationally at the lowest possible level

[958] • The principle of cooperation means that authorities, businesses or agencies have an independent responsibility to ensure the best possible cooperation with relevant actors and businesses in the work of prevention, emergency preparedness and crisis management

[959] St. 5 2020–2021 Social security in an uncertain world Box

[960] Self-preparedness in the event of a power outage

[961] Society is highly dependent on electricity

[962] The power industry is continuously working to maintain a secure supply, but will never be able to guarantee an uninterrupted power supply

[963] It is therefore important that the authorities contribute to realistic expectations regarding the security of electricity supply

[964] It is also necessary for individual end users and vital social actors to become more aware of their own dependence on electricity

[965] Self-preparedness here is about limiting the consequences of power outages

[966] What electricity consumption must be covered in all cases, and what consumption is not as critical

[967] The ambition of the emergency preparedness may be to maintain approximately normal operations and life, or only have the goal of safe evacuation

[968] A middle ground may involve having access to a backup power supply so that it is possible to maintain a minimum of prioritized functions

[969] Self-reliance does not exclude cooperation, quite the opposite

[970] It may be appropriate to analyze and meet your own needs in consultation with nearby stakeholders

[971] In this way, costs can be reduced and common vulnerabilities can be addressed

[972] Critical societal functions should, as far as possible, function even under extraordinary circumstances

[973] Each sector and actor is responsible for assessing their own needs for electricity and ensuring their ability to exercise their responsibilities in the event of a failure of the central power supply

[974] The Directorate for Civil Protection and Emergency Preparedness (DSB) and the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE) are planning a joint project to take a closer look at the self-preparedness of actors who are critically dependent on electricity

[975] For actors who perform critical societal functions, the need for self-preparedness is great, as power supply is a prerequisite for most forms of service provision

[976] In different sectors there are different requirements, different awareness and different incentives related to being prepared for, among other things, power outages, and how this affects the ability to maintain function

[977] Strengthened crosssectoral coordination and clear requirements for self-preparedness in all critically important sectors will be an important means of reducing society's overall vulnerability to loss of power supply or other socially important functions

[978] Priority areas in the work on societal security 2020–

[979] St. 5 Social security in an uncertain world The Covid-19 pandemic The Covid-19 pandemic is the most serious crisis Norway has experienced since the Second World War

[980] The pandemic and the infection control measures that were implemented have had major consequences for all parts of society

[981] This chapter provides a preliminary discussion of the handling of the corona pandemic in Norway, as it stands at the time of the report's presentation

[982] Central elements are the government's strategy for handling the pandemic, the establishment of a knowledge and legal basis for the measures that have been implemented, and the organization and coordination of the government's work

[983] The chapter also points to some of the vulnerabilities that the pandemic has revealed and that the government will consider further as part of its follow-up to the pandemic

[984] The chapter concludes with a discussion of the government's assessments of key challenges in the further handling of the pandemic

[985] During the course of dealing with the pandemic, many decisions have necessarily been made quickly and on an uncertain basis

[986] This increases the possibility that some decisions should have been made differently

[987] It is therefore extra important to learn from the experiences that have been made

[988] This message does not contain an evaluation of the government's handling of the corona pandemic, and only discusses measures that have already been decided

[989] The government has appointed an independent commission to conduct a thorough and comprehensive review and evaluation of the authorities' handling of the coronavirus pandemic

[990] The Corona Commission will map all relevant aspects of the handling

[991] Photo: Fredrik Ringnes, Norwegian Armed Forces

[992] Social security in an uncertain world 5.1 Government policy

[993] – Continue to manage the pandemic so that the disease burden in Norway is low and the health and care services have the capacity to handle the influx of patients

[994] – Continue efforts to get the population to follow basic infection control measures

[995] – Strengthen efforts with testing, isolation, infection tracing and quarantine to detect and control local outbreaks early

[996] – Ensure that the relaxation of infection control measures takes place in a controlled manner, gradually and over time

[997] Consideration for children and young people is prioritized first, followed by consideration for jobs and business

[998] Continue cooperation with the EU to secure vaccines for the population of Norway and contribute to the international effort to ensure all countries have access to vaccines against COVID-19. Continue efforts to build up emergency preparedness capacities for protective equipment, medical equipment and pharmaceuticals in the health and care services. [1003] About the virus, the disease and the spread of infection

[1004] The coronavirus pandemic is the latest of several international outbreaks of infectious diseases

[1005] A number of epidemics of varying severity and scope have occurred in recent decades

[1006] All outbreaks of serious infectious diseases are different, and the consequences are influenced by how contagious and pathogenic the diseases are

[1007] In the 20th century, the Spanish flu was the most serious pandemic, killing between 50 and 100 million people

[1008] In Norway, the Spanish flu took around 15,000 lives

[1009] Other influenza pandemics in the 20th century were the Asian flu of 1957–1958 and the Hong Kong flu

[1010] In the 2000s, the Sars coronavirus caused a global epidemic in 2002–2003, with about 8,000 cases and 774 deaths in 26 countries

[1011] No cases were diagnosed in Scandinavia

[1012] In 2009, the influenza virus A(H1N1) (swine flu) was defined as a pandemic

[1013] Swine flu was a mild illness for most infected people

[1014] It is estimated that 32 people died from this flu in Norway

[1015] In the 2010s, the 2014–2016 Ebola epidemic in West Africa was a serious event that led to over 28,000 cases and 11,000 deaths

[1016] This was the largest Ebola epidemic to date since the virus was discovered

[1017] The outbreak of the coronavirus, which has been named SARS-CoV-2, began in the city of Wuhan in Hubei province, China, in December

[1018] The virus was first detected in humans in January

[1019] On March 11, 2020, the World Health Organization declared the outbreak a pandemic

[1020] The disease caused by the virus has been named COVID-19 (coronavirus disease

[1021] The course of the disease can vary from very mild symptoms to severe illness and death

[1022] Some people develop no symptoms

[1023] The first case of infection in Norway was registered at the end of February

[1024] Until March 10, all reported cases of infection had been traced to abroad, particularly from Italy and Austria, where many Norwegians had been on winter vacation

[1025] After March 10, the virus spread uncontrolled in Norway

[1026] The number of infected people increased, and there were reports that it was not possible to track where more people had become infected

[1027] Therefore, in March, the health authorities, with the support of the Minister of Health and Social Care and the Prime Minister, decided to implement drastic measures to combat the spread of the infection

[1028] The intervention measures helped the crisis go from being a health crisis to becoming a crisis with consequences for all parts of society

[1029] Norway gained control over the spread of the infection in April

[1030] This made it possible to carry out a controlled and gradual phase-out of several of the most intrusive infection control measures

[1031] With better control of the epidemic and a lower number of infected people, the focus could shift from measures that affected everyone to measures to contain the outbreak through basic infection control measures and a targeted effort to suppress outbreaks by finding and isolating infected people, tracing their contacts and quarantining them

[1032] Even with a controlled opening of the 2020–

[1036] The increased infection was met with various measures, primarily at the local level, but some nationwide measures were also introduced, tightening rules on quarantine for close contacts of infected people and banning the serving of alcohol at pubs

[1041] Vaccines A large number of vaccine candidates are under development

[1042] Despite promising data from some early-phase studies, it is still unknown which of these candidates will eventually prove to be safe and effective

[1043] Vaccine development has high risks

[1044] Early access vaccine initiatives must therefore have a portfolio that is broad enough that it is reasonably likely that at least one of the candidates will be successful

[1045] At the same time, it is necessary to make early investments to scale up production to ensure faster access to a sufficient number of doses of those vaccines that will eventually prove to be safe and effective

[1050] ESI), however, Norway will have to be involved through resale agreements that are entered into under equivalent conditions as EU member states

[1055] The starting point is that global solidarity is necessary if we are to succeed in combating the pandemic as quickly as possible

[1056] Since May 2020, the Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunisation (Gavi), the Global Coalition for Epidemic Prevention and Pandemic Prevention (CEPI), and the World Health Organization (WHO) have collaborated to develop a global procurement and distribution system for COVID-19 vaccines

[1057] This mechanism is called COVAX and is a global initiative that will help ensure access to the COVID-19 vaccine in all countries, regardless of ability to pay
