[1112] The government's strategy has been to handle the corona pandemic so that we have control over the spread of infection at all times

[1113] Control means that the burden of disease is low and that the number of patients is manageable in the health and care services, even though the number of sick people may periodically increase and vary between geographical areas

[1114] The containment strategy that the government chose in the early phase of the outbreak led to us gaining control of the spread of the infection in April

[1115] In the spring of 2020, the government therefore switched to a control strategy

[1116] In a controlled manner and over time, the most intrusive measures were replaced in parallel with increased testing, infection tracking and isolation

[1117] At the same time, the health and care services' ability to handle a large number of COVID-19 patients was strengthened

[1118] On May 7, the government presented a long-term strategy and plan for handling the corona pandemic and adjusting measures

[1119] The strategy explains the basis for choosing goals and measures to handle the virus outbreak in Norway

[1120] It is based on three scenarios we should be prepared to handle

[1121] In the first scenario, we have control over the spread of infection and in the long term, intervention measures can be discontinued

[1122] The second scenario involves a sharp increase in the number of sick people, which overloads the capacity of health and care services

[1123] In the third scenario, international cooperation breaks down, and in addition, international supply chains for medical protective equipment and pharmaceuticals, among other things, are weakened

[1124] If this scenario occurs, the strategy and plan will need to be adapted

[1125] When reopening society, it was emphasized that the reopening should be knowledge-based, and that it should take place in a controlled manner, gradually and over time

[1126] Consideration for people in high-risk groups should be given weight and the least intrusive measures should be maintained for the longest time

[1127] Furthermore, it was emphasized that appropriate protective measures against COVID-19 must be in place in all workplaces, and that the risk of infection imported from other countries should be manageable

[1128] When reopening, the concerns of children and young people were prioritized first, followed by concerns for jobs and business

[1129] Better knowledge about the virus and the measures, and increased capacity in testing and infection tracking, with possible subsequent quarantine and isolation, means that we are today significantly better equipped than we were in March to assess how measures can be graded in different infection situations or adjusted to reduce the burden of measures

[1130] We have now learned that waves of infection can be suppressed with measures if the spread of infection increases

[1131] The corona pandemic could last a long time, and the management must therefore be sustainable over time

[1132] The government's goal is that the measures will cause the least possible disruption to society and the economy

[1133] Intervention measures should be scaled down as quickly as possible, but they should also be able to be scaled up again if the infection situation warrants it

[1134] On June 10, 2020, a contingency plan was established with infection control measures that can be implemented in the event of increased spread of infection

[1135] The emergency plan should be a tool and provide a basis for making quick and good decisions if the infection situation makes it necessary to reintroduce measures to prevent the spread of infection (see also section

[1205] Social security in an uncertain world Handling the virus outbreak has required extensive regulatory work

[1206] A number of regulations with temporary duration have been established

[1207] It is being continuously assessed whether there is a need to adjust the regulations in order to meet the development of the pandemic and its management

[1208] As the crisis evolved from primarily being a health crisis to becoming a crisis that encompassed all parts of society, it became necessary to limit the negative consequences of the extensive infection control measures

[1209] An important part of crisis management was about keeping the wheels of society turning

[1210] On March 18, 2020, a proposal for a temporary corona law was presented to the Storting in Prop

[1211] L (2019–

[1212] The proposal aimed to facilitate appropriate and effective measures that were necessary to limit the disruption of normal societal functions as a result of the virus outbreak, and to mitigate negative consequences for the population, business, the public sector or society at large

[1213] According to the proposal, the government would have the authority to adopt regulations that supplemented, supplemented or deviated from current legislation to the extent necessary to safeguard the purpose of the act

[1214] The proposal provided that the Act and regulations issued pursuant to the Act would have a duration of six months, and the proposal allowed a minority in the Storting, with at least one-third of the votes, to fully or partially repeal regulations adopted by the Government

[1215] The proposal was partly inspired by the Emergency Preparedness Act Committee's proposal for a new Emergency Powers Act, which had been subject to broad consultation (see also section

[1216] It is particularly noted that the proposal for a broad mandate was balanced with the possibility for the Storting to repeal adopted regulations with 1/3 of the votes

[1217] At the same time, both the basis and the purpose of the Corona Act were different from the proposal for the Crisis Authorization Act

[1218] While the basis for the Emergency Powers Act was constitutional emergency law, the basis for the Corona Act was the Storting's general delegation authority

[1219] And while the proposed Emergency Powers Act was to apply to all extraordinary crises and was to safeguard critical societal functions or other weighty societal interests, the Corona Act was only to apply in a special situation and had a much broader purpose, namely to limit the disruption of normal societal functions and remedy negative consequences for the population, business, the public sector and society at large

[1220] The proposal was essentially recommended by the special committee to deal with special matters relating to the corona crisis in the committee's unanimous recommendation on 21 March

[1221] Act No. 204 L (2019–2020)), but with some limitations on the government's competence

[1222] Among other things, a clarification was included in the act's purpose statement that clarified a requirement for proportionality for measures under the act

[1223] Furthermore, the government's regulatory competence under the Corona Act was objectively limited to include many specifically specified acts, and the duration of the Corona Act and regulations issued pursuant to the act was reduced from six months to one month

[1224] The committee's recommendation was unanimously approved by the Storting and the law was passed the same day

[1225] The second and final legislative decision was made unanimously on March

[1226] The law was sanctioned by the Cabinet on March 27, 2020, and entered into force on the same day

[1227] On April 21, 2020, the law was extended, with some minor changes, until May 27, 2020, when the Corona Act was repealed

[1228] At the time of repeal, the government had notified the Storting of 32 regulations pursuant to the Act

[1229] To replace the regulations issued pursuant to the Corona Act, the government proposed a number of temporary laws that were adopted and entered into force upon the expiration of the Corona Act

[1230] A number of these laws are in effect until the end of October/beginning of November

[1231] Continuity of critical societal functions

[1232] In addition to coordinating and implementing infection control measures to limit the spread of infection, it has been crucial to keep the wheels turning in critical societal functions such as emergency services, transportation, and the supply of necessary goods (such as groceries

[1235] During the coronavirus pandemic, there have been no reports of the inability of emergency services or rescue services to carry out their missions

[1236] When introducing entry restrictions, exceptions were made for foreigners who are strictly necessary to maintain the proper operation of critical societal functions

[1238] These personnel were offered kindergartens and primary schools for their children, even though the main rule was that kindergartens and primary schools should remain closed

[1239] The Armed Forces' and Civil Defence's exemption schemes have also been important in ensuring normal operations and continuity of critical societal functions

[1266] IMDi's director leads a coordination group consisting of eight central public agencies

[1267] Reporting from the group shows that there is an ongoing need for targeted information for the immigrant population

[1270] The experience from the coordination group will be important for later emergency preparedness work aimed at the immigrant population

[1273] Critical and important societal functions

[1274] In the overview of society's critical functions, a societal function is considered critical if an interruption of seven days or less threatens the population's basic needs

[1275] The corona crisis has shown that during a prolonged crisis, society depends on a number of functions to maintain the safety and welfare of the population

[1276] Measures have been necessary to keep the wheels turning even in businesses that are not included in the established overview of society's critical functions

[1277] The pandemic has shown us that such overviews must be adapted to the nature and duration of the individual crisis

[1278] Examples include child welfare institutions, kindergartens and schools, crisis centers, renovation and cleaning services, and media companies

[1279] These functions are included in the government's expanded list of functions and activities that are considered critical in relation to the corona pandemic

[1280] Guardians working within these functions will be able to be offered a place in kindergarten and primary school

[1281] Societal security in an uncertain world The media and the general public have a legitimate need to understand the background to, and the connection between, the measures being implemented in connection with the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic

[1282] The companies that are central to the handling are also those that receive the most access requests and the most inquiries

[1283] To support a uniform and effective practice during a period of particularly high pressure, a guide was published in April 2020 for ministries and subordinate bodies with advice for handling access requests

[1284] The guide applies to the processing of access in general, and to the processing of access requests in documents relating to the COVID-19 pandemic and the authorities' handling of it, in particular

[1285] The principle of public access and the Public Information Act apply as normal in this situation

[1286] Transparency is a general goal, and a fundamental prerequisite for successfully handling the COVID-19 pandemic

[1287] Managing the COVID-19 pandemic at local and regional levels

[1288] Good cooperation between levels of government has been, and will continue to be, crucial for us to control the virus

[1289] Municipalities have a general responsibility for the safety and security of their own residents and others who are present in the municipalities at any time

[1290] According to the Infection Control Act, municipalities are responsible for assessing the situation and implementing measures to limit the spread of an outbreak and treat the sick

[1291] The corona crisis has been resource-intensive for municipalities

[1292] For smaller municipalities that periodically have many more people than their residents, there is a risk that a major outbreak with many sick people will exceed local capacity

[1293] In August, September and October 2020, several municipalities have had to deal with increased outbreaks of infection, including in Oslo, Bergen, Sarpsborg and Fredrikstad

[1294] The municipalities' work on and follow-up of the TISK strategy (test-isolate-trace-quarantine) has been and is crucial for managing the pandemic over time

[1295] In a letter to the country's mayor dated September 4 from the Minister of Health and Care Services and the Minister of Local Government and Modernization, the municipalities are assured that the government aims to cover all necessary costs in the municipal sector with the follow-up of the TISK strategy and special infection control measures in 2020 and It is also indicated that special compensation will be considered for municipalities that have had large additional expenses as a result of local virus outbreaks

[1296] The county governors support the municipalities in their handling through their guidance and advisory responsibilities, including within health legislation and municipal emergency preparedness obligations

[1297] For example, the county governors have had extensive guidance tasks with regard to the interpretation of the quarantine rules

[1298] The pandemic has also shown the importance of adequate coordination and coordination of power provisions at the national and local levels

[1299] Delegating authority within health preparedness and other areas to local and regional levels can affect our ability to handle major, national incidents

[1300] In March, a number of municipalities adopted local quarantine and entry regulations pursuant to Section 4-1 of the Infection Control Act, and quarantine and infection control regulations were practiced differently between municipalities

[1301] These are drastic measures, both for private individuals, employees, businesses and the public sector

[1302] The introduction of local infection control measures can have national consequences if businesses and important societal functions are severely affected

[1303] To help ensure that national and municipal infection control measures work together and to remove obstacles to the movement of goods and labor between municipalities in Norway, the government issued a guide to municipalities on March 29 regarding local quarantine rules or entry restrictions

[1304] It is important that municipal infection control measures are coordinated with national ones so that everyone is moving in the same direction, while at the same time weighing the measures against other important societal considerations

[1305] If local infection affects several municipalities in a region, the municipalities should coordinate the measures to ensure that the infection control measures constitute a comprehensive response

[1306] An incident with far-reaching consequences

[1307] The coronavirus pandemic has challenged societal security broadly and has had far-reaching consequences for almost all parts of society

[1308] The consequences come from both the direct effects of the coronavirus related to deaths, loss of health, behavioral changes in the population as a result of the pandemic, and the negative societal consequences of infection control measures

[1309] From a societal security perspective

[1310] The corona pandemic has highlighted several risk factors

[1311] Long supply chains for critical goods One risk relates to the vulnerabilities of long and complex supply chains

[1325] Weakening international norms and institutions leads to less stability and predictability

[1326] Cooperation and solidarity are weakened at the expense of the right of the strong

[1337] – Staffing challenges as a result of quarantine regulations and entry restrictions

[1346] Societal security in an uncertain world Capacity and prioritization challenges

[1347] The outbreak of the coronavirus has shown that managing a pandemic, in addition to maintaining normal operational tasks, can create capacity and prioritization challenges

[1348] This can happen both because there is a shortage of certain critical input factors, and because the demand for certain functions increases as a result of the pandemic

[1349] An example is in the health and care services, where COVID-19 patients have partly led to other medical treatment being put on hold

[1350] Other health challenges do not disappear during a pandemic, and with the build-up of preparedness for a larger number of patients with COVID-19, the health service has had to make demanding prioritizations

[1351] The burden on the healthcare personnel who have been involved in handling the incident has been high

[1352] The specialist health service has built up preparedness for more hospital admissions and increased intensive care (including respirators) for patients with COVID-19. Another example is the increased demand for NAV's services

[1353] During the first four weeks after the infection control measures were introduced on March 12, the number of registered job seekers with NAV more than quadrupled

[1354] In the first half of 2020, NAV received more than three times as many applications for unemployment benefits

[1355] as throughout

[1356] During the first week after March 12 alone, NAV received more unemployment benefit applications

[1357] than in all of

[1358] This was mainly due to layoffs, but the number of ordinary unemployed also increased

[1359] At the same time, the contact surface with users was reduced as a result of a number of NAV offices being completely or partially closed

[1360] A number of temporary regulatory changes were also adopted, which led to the need for extensive system adaptations in NAV

[1361] Overall, this has challenged NAV's capacity

[1362] In society at large, increased personnel absence and reduced productivity as a result of the pandemic may reduce the capacity of a number of businesses

[1363] The scope and duration of the coronavirus pandemic could further affect our ability to handle coincident events

[1364] Resources mobilized to deal with the pandemic may have reduced capacity to deal with other concurrent crises

[1365] One example is the Civil Defence, which has been mobilized to assist in handling the corona pandemic while also being a sought-after resource in other incidents, such as forest fires and floods

[1366] In the Emergency Plan for infection control measures in the event of increased infection spread during the COVID-19 pandemic from 10 June, it is considered appropriate that public entities prepare specific emergency plans for how the business can be run as efficiently as possible in a situation where infection control measures are implemented, and that the responsible sector authority takes the initiative to ensure that private entities prepare or have access to corresponding emergency plans

[1367] Risks related to increased use of digital solutions During the corona pandemic, we have also experienced risks related to increased use of digital solutions, such as home office solutions

[1368] In Norway, as in several other countries, the corona pandemic has been used as a theme or "bait" in phishing attempts, which is a term for digital snooping or "fishing" for sensitive information, such as passwords or credit card numbers

[1369] Greater dependence on technological solutions can also lead to a higher risk of data attacks, infrastructure overloads and privacy breaches

[1374] Measures to mitigate the consequences of the coronavirus outbreak The government has worked continuously to address the various challenges that have arisen during the coronavirus pandemic

[1375] Examples include measures to help businesses and the scheme with a school and kindergarten offer for vulnerable children and young people and children of guardians in critical and important social functions

[1376] The scope of the crisis, the uncertainty and the rapid development meant that a number of decisions had to be made at short notice and with great uncertainty

[1377] Some had to be adjusted along the way

[1378] Such an approach has been necessary in a situation where it was not possible to pre-assess all the consequences of measures taken, and where we are constantly gaining new knowledge about the virus and the spread of infection in society

[1379] More about mitigating measures to secure the Norwegian economy and working life

[1380] The corona pandemic has had major consequences for the Norwegian economy and for business, working life and individuals

[1381] Many businesses have been ordered to close or have had to adapt their operations. 2020–

[1382] Societal security in an uncertain world as a result of infection control considerations

[1383] In addition, changes in population behavior have reduced demand for certain goods and services

[1384] The number of layoffs has increased dramatically in many industries

[1385] Several companies have been at risk of losing important expertise during the corona crisis

[1386] The government has aimed to save viable businesses in Norway and provide secure income to employees in the acute situation they found themselves in as a result of the coronavirus outbreak, and has implemented several mitigating measures for Norwegian working life and the economy

[1387] The Government will continue to monitor the economic situation closely and, if necessary, consider measures to support Norwegian businesses and Norwegian workers who have been or are being affected by the corona pandemic

[1388] Up until the time of presentation of this report, the government has worked in three phases on the economic measures resulting from the coronavirus outbreak

[1389] In the first phase, the government and the Storting put in place targeted measures to quickly resolve acute economic challenges, including securing income for employees and providing liquidity to companies to avoid mass layoffs and bankruptcies

[1390] In the second phase, there was a particular focus on supporting industries, individual businesses and small businesses that were particularly hard hit by the coronavirus and the infection control measures

[1391] Targeted measures were also implemented on the education side so that laid-off and unemployed people could quickly gain access to relevant training and education opportunities to improve and further develop their skills

[1392] The third phase has consisted of more general and long-term measures to maintain activity in the economy, and contains a number of measures to get people into work, increase activity in Norwegian business and industry, and contribute to long-term value creation in the private sector going forward

[1393] The virus outbreak has led to more people applying for higher education

[1394] The government's focus on education and skills development ("Education Promise 2020") has allocated funds for 4,000 new study places, with particular emphasis on subject areas that society will need in the years to come, such as health and social sciences, teacher education and ICT-related subjects

[1395] The knowledge base is crucial for good management

[1396] Knowledge of how to best handle the crisis has been crucial

[1397] A good decision-making basis allows us to implement measures that are effective in handling the pandemic, but with the least possible negative consequences for society

[1398] The Norwegian Institute of Public Health and the Norwegian Directorate of Health have been, and are, key knowledge providers for handling the pandemic

[1403] The group emphasized a low disease burden, that the health service is not overloaded, and that negative spillover effects of infection control measures are kept low

[1405] In April, the group received an expanded mandate, which also included consideration of economic measures

[1408] This was to gain an understanding of the effects of the economic measures in interaction with the infection control measures and the infection situation

[1420] International cooperation

[1421] Our national handling of the infection situation is closely linked to what is happening outside our borders

[1471] Preparations in case of increased spread of infection

[1472] The pandemic could be prolonged, and a clear plan is needed if the spread of infection increases

[1473] The emergency plan that was established on June 10, 2020 provides a basis for rapid decisions and a well-considered response if the infection situation makes it necessary to reintroduce measures to prevent the spread of infection (see section

[1474] How and to what extent infection control measures are actually implemented must be assessed specifically based on the current infection situation and updated knowledge

[1475] The goal is to be prepared to implement adequate infection control measures, but also to avoid measures where the costs are high and the infection control effect is small

[1476] Arrangements must be made to detect local outbreaks and larger trends as early as possible

[1477] The effects and costs of various infection control measures must be known to the greatest extent possible so that we are prepared to implement infection control measures when necessary locally, regionally and nationally

[1478] Infection control measures can be implemented individually or in combination, and different infection situations may require different grading of measures and locally limited implementation

[1479] To ensure rapid implementation of necessary infection control measures, the government has also presented a list of possible measures locally, regionally or nationally

[1480] Examples of measures are

[1481] – Measures to protect vulnerable groups

[1482] – Increased encouragement to use home offices

[1483] – Reinforced call to avoid public transport

[1484] – Reduction of maximum numbers in public events

[1485] – Stricter social distancing recommendations at private gatherings

[1486] – Reduced opening hours or closure of service points

[1487] – Encouragement that events take place outdoors

[1488] – Call for more digital teaching at universities

[1489] Sufficient capacity in testing and tracing of infected people Testing, isolation, infection tracing and quarantine (TISK) is central to the Norwegian strategy

[1490] An important contribution to effective control of the pandemic is to conduct infection tracing around confirmed cases of COVID

[1491] By isolating sick people and quarantining close contacts, we can prevent the infection from spreading further from people with or without symptoms and thus quickly stop the further spread of infection in society

[1492] This is important so that we can maintain control of the infection without having to reintroduce the most intrusive measures

[1493] The system for testing and tracking infected people has been systematized and scaled up

[1494] Norway now has an analysis capacity that can meet the needs in a situation with much more infection than what we see today

[1495] In August, some municipalities experienced a large influx of people wanting to test themselves for COVID-19, which caused temporary capacity challenges

[1534] Further strengthening of the knowledge base

[1535] The Norwegian Institute of Public Health has been commissioned to establish a national knowledge program for COVID-19. The program aims to ensure a research-based knowledge base for counseling, patient treatment and key decisions in handling the corona pandemic and its consequences in Norway

[1536] In March, the Norwegian Pandemic Register was established to gain more knowledge about the disease COVID-19, which can be used to improve patient treatment, follow-up of patients, and to find out how patients are doing afterwards

[1537] The registry includes patients admitted to hospital with confirmed COVID-19. The information collected is based on the World Health Organization's reporting form and provides a basis for international comparisons in research on COVID

[1538] Evaluation and learning

[1539] In order to further develop preparedness in Norway, it is crucial to learn from previous crises, both from what went well and what could have been done better

[1540] Instructions for the ministries' work on civil security (the civil security instructions) require that undesirable incidents be evaluated and that identified learning points be followed up

[1541] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security shall ensure that serious incidents, such as the outbreak of the coronavirus, are followed up in the sectors in a systematic manner

[1542] A number of other regulations also require evaluation

[1543] In order to obtain a thorough and comprehensive review and evaluation of the authorities' handling of the corona pandemic, the government has appointed an independent commission

[1544] The commission will look at both the preparedness we had in advance of the pandemic and how the crisis has been handled

[1545] The government has also initiated several research projects to draw lessons from the crisis and build on lessons learned to address future crises

[1546] Societal security in an uncertain world Civil-military cooperation and total defense

[1547] The security policy situation for Norway is changing, cf. point

[1548] This development, combined with increased dependencies between the Norwegian Defence Force and civil society, makes civil-military cooperation increasingly important

[1549] This collaboration clarifies interdependencies related to infrastructure, goods and services, and helps ensure that these dependencies are handled appropriately

[1550] Collaboration is also important for making the best possible use of society's overall resources

[1551] The Total Defence Concept is part of civil-military cooperation, but is limited to encompassing mutual support and cooperation between the Defence Forces and civil society related to crises, from crises in peace to security policy crises and armed conflict

[1552] To help further develop total defence and to strengthen resilience in critical societal functions, the government established the Total Defense Program in 2016 for a duration of four years

[1553] This chapter describes the work completed and the ongoing work to further develop the total defence

[1554] Civil-military cooperation and total defense are also topics in the Ministry of Defense's long-term plan for the defense sector, Bill No

[1570] Civil-military cooperation

[1571] Civil-military cooperation in peacetime is broad, and includes both everyday routine missions and operational ad hoc missions to deal with accidents, natural events and criminal acts such as terrorist attacks

[1572] Several cooperative arenas have been established

[1573] One example is within CBRNE preparedness, where civil and military sides cooperate on the procurement of, among other things, equipment and protective materials and medical evacuation of patients with serious infectious diseases

[1574] Within radiation protection and nuclear emergency preparedness, the Armed Forces contribute with searches, mapping and measurement of radioactivity

[1575] The Armed Forces are also a logistics resource for shipping samples and equipment

[1576] In 2018, 24-hour readiness was established for an analysis laboratory at the Norwegian Defence Research Institute (FFI

[1577] The emergency laboratory ensures emergency and preparedness agencies receive rapid advice and analysis of hazardous substances

[1578] Another area of cooperation is bomb preparedness and explosive ordnance disposal

[1579] This is a specialized field where the expertise is divided between relatively small professional environments in the police and the Armed Forces, respectively

[1580] CBRNE is a general term for incidents that include chemical substances (C), biological agents (B), radioactive substances (R), nuclear material (N) and explosives (E) with high hazard potential

[1581] Social security in an uncertain world

[1582] Examples of civil-military cooperation in peacetime – The Armed Forces can assist the police in a number of specific situations

[1583] Instructions on the Armed Forces' assistance to the police § 3. – The Coast Guard carries out checks on compliance with legislation on behalf of a number of agencies

[1584] – The Coast Guard has operational responsibility for the state tugboat readiness

[1585] – The Coast Guard assists the Norwegian Coastal Administration in the event of acute pollution at sea. – The Armed Forces are an important player in the rescue service

[1586] In addition to participating in the operational resources, the Armed Forces are represented in the rescue management during major operations

[1587] – The rescue helicopter service carries out search and rescue missions, air ambulance missions and other socially beneficial missions following assignments from the Main Rescue Centre

[1588] The rescue helicopters also play a role in the efforts of the police and the Armed Forces in maritime counter-terrorism operations at sea, and when other transport support is needed for the police. – The Armed Forces have a cooperation agreement with the Directorate of Health on strategic air evacuation of patients

[1589] – The Border Guard at the Garrison in Sør-Varanger claims territorial sovereignty in peacetime, and monitors the border and assists the police and the Border Commissariat on the Norwegian-Russian border. – The Home Guard can, among other things, assist the civilian side in natural disasters and as a resource in the rescue service

[1590] – The Armed Forces have assistance missions in explosive ordnance disposal

[1591] The armed forces are assisting with handling, and also supporting the police with special equipment

[1595] Social security in an uncertain world

[1596] The total defense concept Total defense is about ensuring that society's total resources can be used, if necessary, across the entire spectrum of crises, from peace through security policy crises to armed conflict

[1597] This includes both the Defence's support to civil society in crises that affect societal security, and civil society's support to the Defence across the entire spectrum of crises

[1598] Over time, the total defence concept has been adapted to the ever-changing societal challenges, and has proven to be a flexible instrument for good utilization of society's overall resources

[1599] This means that both civilian and military resources can be used to solve existing and new challenges

[1600] Social security and state security are mutually dependent on each other (see section

[1601] The development of the Armed Forces must therefore take place in close collaboration with civilian actors, where civil society's capabilities and prerequisites for supporting the Armed Forces form the basis for the Armed Forces' planning assumptions

[1602] A total defense adapted to new challenges

[1603] Major challenges in our security policy environment, cf. Chapter 3, highlight the importance of total defence for Norway's overall defence capability

[1604] Norway is currently facing a broad, complex threat landscape that increasingly affects across sectors and can challenge the authorities' ability to make good and timely decisions

[1605] Security policy developments are characterized, among other things, by both state and non-state actors using a wider range of instruments

[1606] The development places high demands on Norway's civil and military preparedness, situational awareness, handling ability and resilience

[1607] Civilian support to the Armed Forces The Armed Forces' need for civilian support in the form of services, goods, personnel and access to infrastructure will, in a serious crisis situation and in armed conflict, exceed the resources the Armed Forces need on a daily basis

[1608] Key needs for the Armed Forces will be road, rail, sea and air transport (with associated infrastructure) for the movement of personnel, materiel and supplies, as well as evacuation

[1609] Furthermore, critical factors will be access to fuel, civilian health personnel and health services, pharmaceuticals, medical equipment and more specialized services such as maintenance and engineering services

[1610] Both civilian suppliers that support the Armed Forces, and the Armed Forces themselves, are also dependent on basic services such as power supply, water and, increasingly, civilian ICT infrastructure and services

[1611] Reduced readiness times for military units also mean that support must be able to be in place more quickly

[1612] One of the authorities' primary tasks is to protect the population against crisis and armed conflict

[1613] Although we have come a long way in securing our society, the government recognizes that there is a continuous need to work actively to further develop total defense and to increase the resilience of critical societal functions and fundamental national functions

[1614] Increased resilience in critical societal functions

[1615] Civilian emergency preparedness work and civil-military cooperation have received greater attention in recent years, not only in Norway, but also in NATO and internationally

[1616] The reasons are changes in the threat and risk picture, and that civil preparedness, crisis management and robust critical societal functions are a prerequisite for the individual country's, and thus the alliance's, overall preparedness and defense

[1617] emphasizes to a greater extent the need for resilience in critical societal functions, and an operationalization of Article 3 of the Treaty

[1618] Each NATO member country

[1619] needs to have the resilience

[1620] to withstand shocks like natural disasters, failure of critical infrastructure and military attacks

[1621] Resilience is a society

[1622] ’s ability to resist and recover easily and quickly from these shocks, combining civilian, economic, commercial and military factors

[1623] In sum, resilience is the combination of civil preparedness and military capacity. Against this background, NATO in 2016 adopted expectations for allied nations to build increased resilience within a number of sector-specific areas, cf. the declaration following the Warsaw Summit in July

[1624] In 2016, NATO adopted seven basic expectations for the resilience of member states: – security of continuity of national governance systems and critical public services – robust energy supply – ability to manage uncontrolled movements of people http://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/topics_132722.htm

[1625] Societal security in an uncertain world – robust food and water supply – ability to handle mass casualties – robust communication systems – robust transport systems By increasing the resilience of critical societal functions, the likelihood of major crises hitting Norway is reduced, while at the same time limiting the potential negative consequences such crises may have

[1626] The work on increased resilience within the framework of total defence and NATO's expectations has an important effect within the entire area of ​​societal security

[1627] Together, this increases society's overall resilience and ability to handle crises

[1628] The work of strengthening the robustness of civilian societal functions and civil-military cooperation also contributes as a deterrent factor in a military context

[1629] The seven basic expectations have undergone a preliminary revision, partly based on preliminary experiences from the corona pandemic

[1630] The revised expectations were presented at the NATO Defense Ministerial Meeting in June

[1631] Among the changes was a further emphasis on the importance of robust supply lines

[1632] From the Norwegian side, this is being followed up through continuous work on the seven basic expectations, in which security of supply is also central

[1633] Total defense during the corona pandemic

[1634] Total Defense has been used as part of the response to the coronavirus pandemic

[1635] In handling the pandemic, the Armed Forces have contributed support to the civilian part of the total defense

[1636] Examples include Home Guard assistance for police border control and support to certain hospitals in the form of lending tent solutions to forward reception units

[1637] Several meetings have been held in the Central Total Defence Forum (STF), with participation from all heads of agencies

[1638] The forum has been a central arena for mutual information updates from various sectors

[1639] There has also been extensive use of liaison during the coronavirus response, which has contributed to effective information sharing and proceedings in the sectors

[1640] Requests for assistance to the Armed Forces from civil society, other than the police, were not formally regulated when the country went into lockdown in March

[1641] In order to provide an overall structure for requests for assistance, temporary regulations were established in March 2020 regarding assistance to civil emergency response actors other than the police

[1642] The regulations were based on the Infection Control Act

[1643] Work is underway to establish permanent regulations regarding the Armed Forces' assistance to parties other than the police

[1644] In order to facilitate a holistic approach to the further development of total defence and NATO's expectations of resilient critical societal functions, the government decided in 2016 to establish a programme for the further development of total defence and societal resilience (the Total Defence Programme

[1645] It was a prerequisite when establishing the program that it should be seen in the context of ongoing and relevant work in the ministries and sectors, including the ongoing work on cross-sectoral coordination of social security work and the system for status and condition assessments that was established for the 14 critical societal functions in 2016, cf. section 12.3. The program should not duplicate work already underway, but ensure that this was incorporated into the program where it was considered relevant and appropriate

[1646] The program has a duration

[1647] The program is owned by the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness, and has a steering group consisting of participants from the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness, the Ministry of Defense, the Ministry of Health and Care Services, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries, the Ministry of Petroleum and Energy, the Ministry of Transport, the Ministry of Local Government and Modernization, the Ministry of Agriculture and Food, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs

[1648] Central Total Defense Forum The Central Total Defense Forum is a forum where relevant civilian and military agencies hold regular meetings

[1649] The forum has developed into a central meeting place for discussing various topics and problems within total defense and civil-military cooperation areas

[1650] The forum was used, among other things, to clarify and anchor management roles, responsibilities and authority related to both planning and follow-up of Trident Juncture

[1651] The forum is organized every other year by DSB and the Norwegian Defence Staff

[1652] St. 5 2020–2021 Societal security in an uncertain world The projects in the Total Defence Programme

[1653] The Total Defence Programme has two overarching objectives

[1654] To further develop total defence, including further developing civil authorities' and civil society's support for the Armed Forces, and 2) to strengthen resilience in critical societal functions

[1655] The first objective is being followed up through a project led by the Directorate for Civil Security and Emergency Preparedness (DSB

[1656] The project involves, among other things, assistance to the Armed Forces' planning work and the establishment of plans for civilian support to the Armed Forces in a number of areas

[1657] The project emphasizes that civilian support to the Armed Forces should be integrated to a greater extent into training activities and included in civilian and military training programs

[1658] The project played a central role in planning the civilian participation in the NATO exercises Trident Javelin 2017 and Trident Juncture

[1659] The second objective is followed up by the ministry or sector that is considered to be most affected

[1660] Table 6.1 shows the project structure

[1661] An important part of the work has been to ensure resilience in critical societal functions across the entire spectrum of crises

[1662] During the programme period, certain ministries and sectors have established special projects to delve into specific problems in depth

[1663] The work has contributed to increased awareness of the sectors' role in total defense

[1664] Furthermore, the projects linked to the Total Defence Programme have contributed in several areas to the sectors' work to strengthen deliveries and robustness in critical societal functions and to the assessment of fundamental national functions (see also section

[1665] In several sectors, the dialogue with the police and the Norwegian Defence Forces regarding the security of objects has been strengthened, and the recognition of the need for self-preparedness related to the delivery of particularly critical services has increased

[1666] The work of developing and revising relevant planning has been central in several sectors, as has the revision and preparation of regulations that include provisions related to security policy crises and armed conflict

[1667] An example of a project is the Ministry of Transport's project on "Transport in Total Defence

[1668] The project was established in the fall of 2017 as four sectoral meeting series within aviation, railways, roads/public transport and coastal/sea, with participation from both civilian and military sides

[1669] The project has aimed to map the status and identify needs for further developing transport systems based on NATO's expectations, and to further clarify and follow up on the Armed Forces' needs and expectations for civil transport, including measures in the civil emergency preparedness system (SBS) that deal with the Armed Forces' access to civil transport resources and civil transport infrastructure and services

[1670] The project has come a long way in clarifying the Armed Forces' needs for civilian transport infrastructure and services, and has initiated the preparation of relevant regulations for legislation in the transport sector

[1671] Questions remain related to the Armed Forces' need for and use of civilian transport resources and transporters in various types of scenarios

[1672] The project planned for further clarification of this in 2020, but has been somewhat delayed due to the corona situation

[1673] As also highlighted in section 6.6, it has not been the intention to put an end to the work on further developing civil-military cooperation in the transport area because the period for the Total Defence Programme is ending

[1674] The work is long-term, and will require continuous adaptation beyond

[1675] Overall, the establishment of the Total Defence Programme has been a driving force in the work to further develop and modernise total defence

[1676] The projects in the program have contributed to increased knowledge and expertise about roles, responsibilities and authority related to security crises and armed conflict

[1677] Exercise Trident Juncture 2018 In the fall of 2018, Norway was the host nation for NATO's high-profile military exercise

[1678] The exercise is described as the largest NATO exercise in recent times, with participation from 31 nations, approximately 50,000 people, 250 aircraft and helicopters, 65 vessels and 10,000 vehicles

[1679] The exercise required significant preparation and effort both before, during and after the exercise

[1680] NATO's objective with the exercise was to demonstrate and practice the alliance's ability to plan and execute a joint military operation in line with Article 5 of the Atlantic Treaty against an equal adversary

[1681] From the Norwegian side, a central objective was to train in the reception of allied reinforcements on a large scale, test the host nation support concept, national planning, and total defense

[1682] More than 50 civilian Norwegian agencies participated

[1683] Trident Juncture 2018 was two-part with a full-scale exercise (LIVEX) and a command post exercise (CPX

[1684] The full-scale exercise involved extensive host nation support from Norwegian civil authorities to ensure the safe and secure movement of the participating allied forces, including both personnel and materiel, into and out of the exercise area

[1685] Section 5 Social Security

[1686] in an uncertain world Planning for and receiving NATO forces and materiel was a comprehensive contingency event for the military and civilian parts of the total defense

[1687] supported the Norwegian Defence in the planning and implementation of the exercise

[1688] DSB was responsible for coordinating the civilian efforts related to the reception, stay and return of military personnel and equipment

[1689] The planning used existing and established new collaborative arenas that have increased mutual knowledge and understanding of each other's areas of responsibility, roles and needs

[1690] From January to November 2018, DSB organized collaboration conferences to ensure that the involved authorities at directorate level were coordinated among themselves, and with the Armed Forces, in planning host country support

[1691] The cooperative conferences focused on mutual information sharing, and facilitated the ability of civilian agencies to raise issues and challenges throughout all phases of the planning and execution of the full-scale exercise

[1692] County governors affected by the full-scale exercise Trident Juncture 2018 were an integral part of the Armed Forces and DSB's preparations and implementation of host country support

[1693] The county governors further followed up with affected municipalities and helped to elevate relevant issues from the regional and local level into the established coordination arenas

[1694] The planning and implementation of the full-scale exercise has given the civilian and military parts of the total defence a unique opportunity to work on further developing plans for host country support, while at the same time experiencing what receiving allied forces from NATO entails in practice

[1695] Good planning and close civil-military cooperation were of great importance for the successful implementation

[1696] Following the full-scale exercise, NATO and its member states conducted a command post exercise

[1697] This is an exercise where staffs and commands/crisis management in participating agencies were trained in handling security policy crises and defending Norway

[1698] In connection with the exercise, an extensive competency course was conducted to ensure that both civilian and military authorities were given the best possible conditions to succeed in handling the issues they encountered in the exercise

[1699] The exercise helped Norway train in handling and cooperation between civil and military authorities at all levels in a situation in Norway where NATO's Article 5 is triggered

[1700] CPX raised issues related to, among other things, prioritization and allocation of resources, establishment of situational pictures and situational understanding, sharing and handling of classified information, and legal issues related to, among other things, emergency preparedness regulations and the international law of war

[1711] Social security in an uncertain world Lessons from the exercise

[1712] The main conclusion after the exercise is that it was successful

[1713] This also seems to be the general opinion at all levels

[1714] NATO's evaluation report praises Norway as a host nation

[1715] The primary Host Nation was outstanding

[1716] Norway's Total Defense Concept and related plans meant that they had the will, civilian and military teamwork and means to make

[1717] Trident Juncture 2018 LIVEX a success

[1718] Norway saw LIVEX as an opportunity to test and adjust their planning, particularly their ability to receive NATO

[1719] the event of a crisis

[1720] The civilian support for national and allied military forces was crucial for the participants in Trident Juncture to benefit from the exercise

[1721] Professional planning and implementation were also of great importance for Norway's reputation as a credible ally both within and outside NATO

[1722] A number of evaluations have been carried out following the exercise

[1723] The individual sectors have conducted their own evaluations, and a cross-sectoral evaluation has been conducted, the Norwegian Defence has conducted its evaluations, and the Norwegian Defence Research Institute has conducted an overall civil-military assessment of the exercise

[1724] The conclusions from the overall experience report confirm that the exercise was largely successful for Norway

[1725] “Trident Juncture 2018 has contributed to Norwegian security in several ways

[1726] Firstly, the exercise has contributed to drawing the Alliance's attention to the High North and to our allies gaining knowledge and experience in operating in Norwegian areas

[1727] Secondly, NATO and Norway as the host country have balanced the concern to preserve the High North as a low-tension region, especially with regard to relations with Russia, through early warning, openness, transparency and fulfillment of international agreements

[1728] At the same time, the exercise has helped to demonstrate NATO's will and ability for collective defense and thereby contributed to credible deterrence

[1729] The national benefit of the exercise is linked to several factors

[1730] The Norwegian Armed Forces have exercised together with NATO, both the command structure and tactical units in the field

[1731] Trident Juncture 2018 has provided an opportunity to practice and train the reception of allied reinforcements on a large scale, in addition to testing the total defense concept and the national planning and practical implementation of host nation support

[1732] The exercise has been a catalyst for increased cooperation in total defense and has revitalized the entire total defense effort

[1733] The evaluation reports from national actors and NATO show that the exercise objectives were largely achieved

[1734] A number of learning points have been identified and are being included in the further process of experience management

[1735] Trident Juncture 2018 has been both time- and resource-intensive, but has contributed to a boost for total defense.”

[1736] The evaluation reports nevertheless point to several areas that military and civilian total defence actors should work together to improve and further develop in the follow-up work after the exercise

[1737] These include establishing a common situational understanding between civilian and military total defense actors, assessing the need for establishing a total defense council, further developing the host country support concept, closer and more coordinated civil-military cooperation on exercises, further developing the ability to share classified information, strengthening total defense at the local and regional level, strengthening private-public cooperation within the framework of total defense, and strengthening coordination of civil and military planning processes

[1738] The way forward

[1739] In recent years, a lot of work has been done to strengthen total defense efforts on the civilian side, including through the establishment of the Total Defense Program and through Norway's role as host nation for exercise Trident Juncture

[1740] Although work on total defence on the civilian side has come a long way, both societal developments and a constantly changing threat landscape mean that the design of total defence requires continuous adaptation

[1741] Trident Juncture 2018 served as a good benchmark to test how far we have come in our work with civilian support for the Armed Forces

[1742] The exercise provided important contributions to further prioritization

[1743] Through the work in the Total Defence Programme, points have been identified that require special follow-up beyond the programme period which is ending

[1744] As a follow-up to the Total Defence Programme, a contact group will be established at ministry level for total defence work

[1745] The contact group will ensure coordination of the total defense work, and help identify challenges

[1746] Continued prioritization of total defense work also requires that the directorates and agencies in the sectors continue their efforts in the area, and this is based on

[1747] that ministry- 2020–2021 Meld

[1748] Social security in an uncertain world The ministers ensure the necessary prioritization in the sectors

[1749] Coordination and coordination

[1750] The larger cross-sectoral exercises in recent years have, to a greater or lesser extent, included an element of civil-military cooperation

[1751] In some of the exercises where the crisis has been at the upper end of the crisis spectrum, the Ministry of Defence has functioned as the lead department

[1752] In these cases, the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, with the Crisis Support Unit (KSE), has supported the lead ministry with coordination of cross-sectoral reporting and a composite situational picture from the civilian sectors

[1753] Furthermore, the Ministry of Justice and Public Security has been responsible for coordinating civil preparedness and crisis management in the other ministries

[1754] The relationship between the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness' coordination role during crises and the tasks of the lead department in central crisis management will be specified in the civil security instructions

[1755] DSB has a central coordinating role in several areas

[1756] Among other things, DSB will assist the Ministry of Justice and Public Security and relevant sector ministries on the civilian side in coordinating the handling of major crises and disasters

[1757] If an incident requires coordination on the civilian side, such as scenarios such as Trident Juncture 2018, the Ministry of Justice and Public Security and DSB initiate reporting from the county governors and the municipality through a coordination channel

[1758] DSB also facilitates information sharing at directorate/agency level

[1759] This coordination role of DSB was highlighted as a useful instrument in the evaluation from Trident Juncture

[1760] Situational awareness Establishing a situational awareness involves perceiving individual events, seeing different events in KSE supports

[1761] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security's coordinating role in the area of civil security and is a permanent point of contact for information to and from the Ministry of Justice and Public Security in the event of extraordinary incidents and crises

[1762] If necessary, KSE must be able to provide support to the management department and the Crisis Council in their crisis management

[1763] KSE is the secretariat for the Crisis Council

[1766] Royal decree 24 June

[1767] Instructions for the Directorate of Civil Protection and Emergency Preparedness coordinating roles

[1768] Societal security in an uncertain world context, and interpret and assess these in such a way as to create an understanding of the situation's significance and potential development for affected individuals, businesses and societal functions

[1769] This applies both in a normal situation and during crises

[1770] Situational awareness requires both access to information (including intelligence, reporting and information sharing) and the ability to utilize the information, including analytical expertise and capacity

[1771] A good understanding of the situation adapted to the responsibilities an actor has is a prerequisite for being able to make timely and good decisions, especially in complex situations

[1772] Furthermore, situational understanding requires that there are good and timely reporting and coordination routines, both between sectors and levels of administration

[1773] Experience from exercises, especially Trident Juncture 2018, shows that it is demanding to establish a common civil-military situational understanding, as well as to assess expected developments and which measures should be implemented

[1774] Depending on roles, responsibilities, authority and societal mission, the actors involved will need different information

[1775] The weighting of available information may also vary

[1776] Sharing the actors' understanding is therefore important in order to form the basis for a common understanding of the situation between different actors

[1777] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security will further develop the ability to establish, maintain and analyze a cross-sectoral situational picture at a strategic level on the civilian side

[1778] The Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness will, together with the Ministry of Defence, assess how the civil and military situational picture can together improve the overall national situational understanding, and the two ministries will also further develop their cooperation on the dissemination of threat and risk information

[1779] The establishment of a "total defense council

[1780] In a war theatre, military authorities can take over the supreme leadership of the police and, if necessary, also of other civilian branches of administration, cf. the Act on Special Measures during War, Danger of War and Similar Circumstances (the Emergency Preparedness Act

[1781] A theater of war is an area where hostilities are taking place or can be assumed to be imminent

[1782] Based on experiences from, among other things, exercise Trident Juncture 2018, the government will assess the need for a multidisciplinary "total defense council" at agency and directorate level in situations where a theater of war has been established

[1783] The purpose will be for the Chief of Defence, within the authority granted to him, to be able to carry out appropriate coordination and task prioritisation towards civilian agencies and administrative bodies, without the Defence having to take over their management

[1784] The Council will be able to function in situations where a theatre of war has been established, and will be limited to the areas of expertise and the authority that the participants in the Council represent, and the decision-making authority that the Chief of Defence has been given in the theatre of war

[1785] The Norwegian Armed Forces, in collaboration with civilian agencies, have developed a national concept for host country support

[1786] The concept describes how Norway as a nation will receive and support allied reinforcements, including the roles, responsibilities and authority of civilian and military actors at central and regional levels

[1787] A first version of the concept was developed and tested during the NATO exercise Trident Juncture

[1788] The concept was revised in the fall of 2019 in line with experience gained from the exercise

[1789] The concept is an important framework for further development of plans for host country support in the various sectors

[1790] The work on the host nation support concept is highlighted as one of the most important factors in making Trident Juncture 2018 a success, including through clarifications of roles, responsibilities and authorities across sectors and identification of the need for civilian support for the Armed Forces when receiving allied reinforcements

[1791] At the regional level, triangular cooperation between the county governor, the police and the Home Guard is central to the coordination of host country support

[1792] There is a continuing need to implement the concept in civil planning for relevant sectors at multiple levels

[1793] This is followed up, among other things, in the allocation letter to the county governor

[1794] Increased liaison

[1795] Exercise Trident Juncture 2018 demonstrated the importance of liaison between civilian and military actors at agency level to ensure better understanding of roles, responsibilities and authority, as well as contribute to the efficient flow of information between the actors

[1796] The liaison helped ensure that incidents could be handled quickly

[1797] They also contributed to a better understanding of the situation as a basis for necessary priorities

[1798] It is an advantage if businesses that provide liaison to the Norwegian Defence Forces' operational headquarters according to plans participate in the Norwegian Defence Forces' annual exercises Polaris and Gram

[1799] The liaison arrangement is considered an important tool

[1800] St. 5 Social security in an uncertain world

[1801] Closer civil-military cooperation on exercises

[1802] Exercises help build competence and insight into the responsibilities and roles of civilian and military actors, and provide a basis for improving planning, preventive measures and crisis management mechanisms

[1803] Exercises are also a key tool for further developing and institutionalizing knowledge about actors in total defense and for developing collaborative relationships

[1804] Mutual involvement in exercises is important for further developing total defense at all levels

[1805] In the past three years, three major exercises have been carried out where the civilian side has participated in both the planning and implementation of the exercises

[1806] Trident Javelin in 2017, Trident Juncture in

[1807] and Trident Jupiter

[1808] Crucial to organizing an exercise of the magnitude of Trident Juncture 2018 is the established civil-military cooperation within the framework of the total defense concept

[1809] Annual activities are held where individual elements of total defense are practiced

[1810] In order for the total defense to function as a whole, larger total defense exercises should also be arranged at regular intervals

[1811] The purpose is to further develop civil-military cooperation

[1812] The exercises should include relevant total defence actors at several levels of administration

[1813] Furthermore, participation from voluntary organizations and private actors with responsibility for critical societal functions and critical infrastructure should be considered

[1814] It is a goal that civilian support to the Armed Forces should be integrated to a greater extent into training activities, and included in both civilian and military training programs

[1815] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security will develop a system that will contribute to better coordination and planning of exercise activities, both within its own sector and across sectors

[1816] Effective and secure communication between total defense actors is of great importance, among other things, for information sharing, collaboration and common situational understanding

[1817] Work has been underway for several years to achieve such solutions

[1818] The Total Defence Programme has been a driving force for actors in total defence to be better able to communicate effectively and securely on both unclassified and classified communication systems

[1819] The program has contributed to providing an overview of which actors need to communicate with each other, which systems these actors have access to, and improving competence in using the systems

[1820] Together with the rollout of systems, this has contributed to more efficient and secure communication

[1821] Some players have also entered into contingency agreements for the use of systems from other players in geographical proximity, while other players have invested in establishing new systems

[1822] Despite positive developments in recent years, the evaluations of Trident Juncture 2018 show that competence and access to graded communication platforms still vary among total defence actors

[1823] This shows that there is still a need for increased attention to graded communication, particularly at the regional and local level, and with private actors in total defense

[1824] Local and regional level

[1825] County governors, municipalities and a number of other regional and local agencies have important roles in the Norwegian total defense

[1826] In the first period of the Total Defence Programme, a lot of work has been carried out at the central level

[1827] The results of the work have been disseminated and integrated to a lesser extent into regional and local social security work throughout the period

[1828] There is therefore much work remaining regionally and in the municipalities

[1829] Today, only a few municipalities and county governors have mapped risk and vulnerability, or planned for preparedness related to events at the upper end of the crisis spectrum

[1830] Large geographical variations are also recorded

[1831] Nevertheless, regional and local projects have been initiated that have worked on specific areas within total defense

[1832] In particular, the triangular cooperation between the county governor, the Home Guard and the police is central to the regional total defence cooperation, both with regard to prevention, planning and handling

[1833] To ensure that the work done at the national level reaches regions and municipalities and that the work done in the regional and local projects has transfer value to other areas, DSB has established a working group with special responsibility for disseminating knowledge and developing total defense to county governors and municipalities

[1834] The goal is to incorporate total defense thinking as an integrated part of their work on societal security

[1835] Learning points after Trident Juncture 2018 are part of this

[1836] The results of the work at the regional and local level contribute to improving competence, clarifying roles, responsibilities and authority in a security crisis, and modernising total defence regionally and locally

[1837] More specifically, the work will contribute to

[1838] Social security in an uncertain world

[1839] – Establishing a comprehensive understanding of roles, responsibilities and authority in total defence among county governors and municipalities

[1840] – That county governors and municipalities include events across the entire crisis spectrum in their public security work, including in risk and vulnerability analyses, emergency plans and exercises. – That regional and local civil-military exercises are carried out in which county governors and municipalities are involved. – That public-private cooperation is integrated into regional and local total defence. – That it is arranged so that projects that contribute to the further development of total defence in a region or municipality have transfer value to other geographical areas

[1841] Public-private collaboration

[1842] Civilian support for national and allied forces is crucial to the country's defense capability, while also safeguarding the basic functions of society

[1843] The main principle today when it comes to civilian support for the Armed Forces is that it is based on commercial arrangements, requisition (preferably prepared requisition) and cooperation with civil emergency preparedness to the greatest extent possible

[1844] The Norwegian Armed Forces are currently dependent on private suppliers and owners of critical infrastructure and critical societal functions

[1845] The civilian side has a responsibility to facilitate the proper operationalization of this support, and to the extent possible, to ensure that both planned and unforeseen needs from Norwegian and allied military forces can be met

[1846] Furthermore, the Armed Forces and the civilian side have a joint responsibility to ensure that any vulnerabilities related to dependency are identified and reduced. The extensive work that has been done in recent years to revitalize preparations for civilian support to the Armed Forces must continue

[1847] At the same time, the Norwegian Defence Force will increasingly identify and make visible its needs for support from civilian actors

[1848] Since private

[1849] Since private actors own a large share of the critical functions that both the Armed Forces and civil society depend on, it is important to find solutions to include private enterprises in planning in the event of crises and armed conflict

[1850] On the civilian side, several sectors in the total defense have close collaboration with private suppliers

[1851] The cooperation is followed up in the sectors and in cooperation between the individual sector and the Armed Forces

[1852] Public-private cooperation in total defense nevertheless has some common issues

[1853] Among other things, cooperation in total defense is based largely on society's ability to share information, even when the information is classified according to the Security Act

[1854] When developing graded communication solutions, it is important to take into account the needs of the total defense and the civilian side

[1855] The Safety Act is discussed in more detail in chapter

[1856] Furthermore, increased use of civilian suppliers within the framework of total defence may in the long term contribute to international law challenges as discussed in box 6.4, and these challenges must be taken into account in public-private cooperation

[1857] To help ensure that private businesses also know what is expected of them in a crisis situation, private businesses should be integrated as participants in military, civilian and civilmilitary exercises

[1858] Participation in exercises creates good relationships, networks and understanding of each other's roles, responsibilities and authority

[1859] Exercises can also be a tool for uncovering vulnerabilities

[1861] Through the work of further developing the total defence's ability to safeguard civil support for the Armed Forces, issues related to resource allocation have been identified, including the ability for effective decision-making processes and the sectors' ability to operationalise prioritisation mechanisms at all levels

[1862] In a security crisis, there will be a shortage of resources and it will be challenging to prioritize between different civilian needs and between civilian and military needs

[1863] This applies to resources in the form of materials, personnel, infrastructure, logistics and supplies

[1864] Appropriate prioritization requires

[1866] The County Governor has an important coordinating role in civil-military cooperation in the county

[1867] This includes, among other things, planning civilian support for the Armed Forces in line with the total defense concept, and military support for civilian society during undesirable incidents in peacetime

[1870] St. 5 Social security in an uncertain world a comprehensive overview of dependencies
