[3058] Section 5 Societal security in an uncertain world finds security work across sectors in the municipality

[3059] The work will reduce the risk of loss of life, health, the environment and material assets

[3060] Municipalities are subject to a number of sectoral laws that impose social security requirements on the municipalities

[3061] The provisions on municipal emergency preparedness obligations give the municipality the role of local coordinator through statutory obligations

[3062] These duties consist of the municipality using special instruments to promote: – comprehensive and systematic social security work – a cross-sectoral perspective – collaboration with other social security actors Knowledge of risk and vulnerability is the basis for good municipal social security work

[3063] Holistic Risk and Vulnerability Analysis (RVA) is developed on the basis of RVA analyses from the various sectors, and provides municipalities with a basis for seeing connections between these

[3064] Based on the comprehensive ROS analysis, the municipality will prepare an overall emergency preparedness plan

[3065] This shall coordinate and integrate other emergency preparedness plans in the municipality, and be coordinated with other relevant public and private crisis and emergency preparedness plans

[3066] The regulations on municipal emergency preparedness also give the municipality the obligation to integrate and follow up on public safety in plans pursuant to the Planning and Building Act

[3067] DSB conducts an annual municipal survey

[3068] An important prerequisite for good municipal social security work is to have an overview and knowledge of risk and vulnerability in the municipality

[3069] DSB's survey shows that there has been a positive development in the work on municipal emergency preparedness obligations for several years and that an increasing number of municipalities are meeting the requirements for comprehensive risk and vulnerability analyses, emergency preparedness plans and exercises

[3070] In 2020, a full 98 percent of municipalities state that they have implemented comprehensive ROS

[3071] However, the quality of the analyses carried out varies

[3072] Regulations on municipal emergency preparedness obligations set some minimum requirements for the comprehensive ROS analysis

[3073] Overall, 61 percent of municipalities have comprehensive ROS that meet selected requirements

[3074] This is approximately at the same level as in previous years

[3075] The municipal survey shows that the greatest potential for improvement still lies in having updated plans

[3076] In order to work systematically and holistically with societal security, goals and a plan for follow-up must be developed

[3077] In the 2020 municipal survey, 8 out of 10 municipalities responded that they have prepared goals for their work on public safety and emergency preparedness, and nearly 8 out of 10 municipalities said they have a plan for follow-up

[3078] Furthermore, the results show that municipalities are using the Planning and Building Act too little as an active tool to safeguard public safety

[3079] An important indicator of the quality of community safety work is that it is rooted in the municipality's administrative and political leadership

[3080] By facilitating the municipal council's consideration of a comprehensive ROS analysis and follow-up plan and overall emergency preparedness plan, it is also facilitated for the municipal management to take a position on important public safety issues

[3081] In 2018, DSB published a new guide to regulations on municipal emergency preparedness obligations

[3082] An important purpose of the guide has been to clarify the relationship between municipal emergency preparedness obligations and other work on public safety in the municipality and under the auspices of external emergency preparedness actors

[3083] DSB has also prepared a guide for public safety in municipal spatial planning, and a separate guide on how to ensure public safety and climate adaptation in planning according to the Planning and Building Act

[3084] The municipality as a planning authority The Planning and Building Act is the central tool for ensuring good planning

[3085] As the local planning authority, the municipality has the final responsibility for plans pursuant to the Planning and Building Act

[3086] The consideration of public safety is enshrined in the law, which requires municipalities to “prevent the risk of loss of life, damage to health, the environment and important infrastructure, material assets, etc.” Promoting public safety in municipal planning involves making a comprehensive assessment of the impact that spatial plans may have on society and the population

[3087] The best way to prevent damage is to avoid building in hazardous areas

[3088] The Planning and Building Act requires the implementation of ROS analyses and impact assessments related to area plans

[3089] Municipalities are responsible for ensuring that the hazards are mapped, assessed and taken into sufficient consideration when plans are adopted

[3090] Through regulations on consideration zones, municipalities introduce legally binding restrictions such as building bans or special requirements for development of the area to ensure that public safety is maintained

[3091] Climate change is challenging land use, among other things due to rising sea levels, increased frequency of floods, etc

[3092] Planning and Building Act Section 3-1 letter h

[3093] Public safety in planning and construction case processing

[3094] Social security in an uncertain world of floods and landslides and problems with stormwater in densely populated areas

[3095] The Planning and Building Act sets requirements for assessing the risk of natural damage in all planning and construction activities in Norway, and gives the municipality the opportunity to direct new development to areas that are less vulnerable to climate change or where measures can be implemented in advance that make the area less vulnerable

[3096] Spatial planning is central to preventing loss and damage due to floods and landslides

[3097] New state planning guidelines for climate and energy planning and climate adaptation were adopted in September

[3098] Here, the guidelines for climate and energy planning from 2009 were expanded to also include climate adaptation

[3099] The purpose of the guidelines is that municipalities, county authorities and the state, through their planning, should, among other things, contribute to limiting or avoiding the effects of climate change

[3100] To be on the safe side, work on climate adaptation should be based on high alternatives from national climate projections when assessing the consequences of climate change

[3101] Supplementary guidance to the guidelines was completed in the autumn

[3102] The guide will help municipalities to take climate considerations into account in their planning work

[3103] It is also relevant for other levels of government and private actors who perform services for the administration or develop proposals for plans

[3104] The Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE) assists municipalities and other stakeholders in managing risks related to floods and landslides

[3105] NVE's assistance is linked to spatial planning, mapping, security measures, warning/monitoring and emergency preparedness

[3106] Every four years, the government will prepare national expectations for regional and municipal planning

[3107] NVE can raise objections to plans that are contrary to national and significant regional interests within NVE's areas of responsibility

[3108] Monitoring and warning of floods and landslides

[3109] It is neither economically profitable nor practically possible to physically secure all buildings exposed to flooding and landslides

[3110] Precipitation is a significant cause of floods, landslides and mudslides

[3111] Climate change, especially increased precipitation overall and in the form of torrential rain, is also making it more demanding to map hazards and secure areas

[3112] Through monitoring, model calculations and warnings of precipitation, flood and avalanche hazards, appropriate emergency response resources can be activated in time to save lives and movable assets

[3113] In addition, the warning service leads to a general increase in awareness of flood and avalanche danger

[3114] NVE is responsible for the national flood and avalanche warning service, which is operated in collaboration with the Norwegian Meteorological Institute (MET) and the Norwegian Public Roads Administration

[3115] The service includes flood warning, landslide warning, avalanche warning, ice warning (for water and rivers) and monitoring and warning of large mountain avalanches

[3116] The landslide and avalanche warning services were launched in 2013 and were developed in collaboration with MET, the Norwegian Public Roads Administration and the then Norwegian Rail Administration (now Bane NOR

[3117] It is up to local actors to assess monitoring and warning of specific valley sides and landslide paths

[3118] Monitoring and warning are important elements in preparedness against landslides

[3119] The monitoring of large unstable mountain areas in Norway is carried out by NVE

[3120] The objects are risk classified by the Geological Survey of Norway (NGU) on behalf of the NVE

[3121] The risk classification and a socio-economic cost/benefit assessment are used to determine the level of monitoring

[3122] When the danger level changes, NVE notifies emergency response actors such as municipalities, the police and the county governor, and follows up with geotechnical situation reports

[3123] In line with the principle of responsibility and cooperation, NVE assists other actors, primarily the police and municipalities, in handling flood and landslide incidents

[3124] This primarily involves professional advice, for example related to the need for evacuation or other measures, but also the implementation of physical measures

[3125] Safety measures against floods and landslides Physical safety measures can reduce the risk in certain areas where a high flood and landslide risk has been identified for existing buildings

[3126] NVE's assistance scheme is intended to help municipalities with security measures where the challenges are so great that it is not reasonable to place the responsibility on the individual resident or the municipality

[3127] The main purpose of the scheme is to assist municipalities professionally and financially in planning with the aim of prevention, and to secure existing buildings against flood and landslide damage

[3128] NVE provides assistance either by itself investigating, planning and implementing the construction of security measures or by providing subsidies to the municipality, which in that case carries out the measure itself

[3129] In both cases, the municipality is the project owner according to the provisions of the Planning and Building Act

[3130] Securing existing buildings is not an obligation, neither for the owner, the municipality nor for the state

[3131] NVE prioritizes assistance according to risk, i.e. the degree of danger and consequences for damage to existing buildings and danger to life and health

[3132] The measures where investment in security will provide the greatest co- NVE report no. 77-2016. 2020–

[3133] Social security in an uncertain world, the economic benefit in relation to the costs is prioritized

[3134] In 2020, approximately NOK 370 million was allocated to NVE's assistance scheme for ordinary security measures, of which NOK 165 million was allocated in measure packages in connection with the COVID-19 pandemic

[3135] It is important that the scheme does not undermine the responsibility of the municipality and developers to ensure safety against floods and landslides in new construction

[3136] Assistance is therefore not provided for security, which is a direct prerequisite for a building permit

[3137] In the case of existing developments, NVE's share of the financing may be reduced if greater consideration should have been given to the risk of flooding or landslides when establishing the development, and the municipality or developer may be held responsible for this

[3138] NVE's share of the financing can also be reduced if the security measure, in addition to securing existing buildings, also facilitates new development

[3139] Details about compensation schemes for natural damage

[3140] Certain areas in Norway are particularly exposed to natural disasters

[3141] In coastal areas, storm and landslide damage predominate, while lowlands are more susceptible to flood damage

[3142] Figures from Finance Norway and the Norwegian Natural Disaster Pool showed that compensation payments after natural disasters in 2019 amounted to over half a billion kroner

[3143] With certain exceptions, buildings and movable property in Norway that are insured against fire are also automatically covered against natural damage

[3144] The natural damage insurance scheme ensures broad access to insurance against natural damage

[3145] Insurance companies that are obliged to compensate for natural damage must be members of the Norwegian Natural Damage Pool

[3146] The pool determines the premium rate and equalizes insurance payments between the insurance companies

[3147] The natural disaster insurance scheme is based on a solidarity principle, which means that the premium is set at the same rate regardless of the risk of natural disaster

[3148] Everyone therefore has the opportunity to obtain natural damage insurance regardless of where the building is located

[3149] In the Revised National Budget 2019, the government announced that it would consider whether conflicting considerations warrant a review of the scheme

[3150] The natural disaster insurance scheme, with its solidarity principle, is an important part of society's preparedness against natural disasters

[3151] The Government therefore believes that the main principles of the scheme should remain in place, and that Box 10.2 Landslide and flood protection in Longyearbyen Climate change has led to a greater risk of landslides in Longyearbyen

[3160] NVE is currently constructing parts of the security measures

[3170] Organization of Norwegian natural disaster insurance – About the Norwegian Natural Disaster Pool

[3171] The Ministry of Local Government and Modernisation may allocate discretionary funds to municipalities and county municipalities that have incurred expenses for natural damage or other extraordinary events

[3172] This may be for handling the acute crisis situation, cleaning up and/or returning municipal infrastructure to its original standard

[3173] As a general rule, the discretionary funds shall be used for the reconstruction of critical municipal infrastructure, such as municipal roads, water and sewage networks and other infrastructure on which the municipality depends in order to perform its statutory tasks

[3174] The Ministry will assess in each individual case whether the infrastructure is considered to be part of the critical infrastructure

[3175] The scheme is intended to ensure that individual municipalities do not incur disproportionate expenses following natural disasters, and that the costs of reconstruction do not affect the other services provided to residents

[3176] Municipalities and county authorities are responsible for the infrastructure themselves and they are also responsible for emergency preparedness and reconstruction in the event of natural damage

[3177] The compensation scheme ensures that they receive partial compensation for the expenses incurred in the event of major incidents, so that they have a safety net

[3178] Reconstruction shall only take place to the original standard, but compensation may be provided for raising the standard if newer building regulations etc. indicate that the standard must be raised

[3179] The State Natural Damage Scheme is the state's own compensation scheme aimed at private individuals

[3180] It covers damage to assets that cannot be insured through ordinary private insurance

[3181] Examples of assets that cannot be insured through a general insurance scheme are facilities for industry, sports and tourism, quays and breakwaters, agricultural land and private roads and bridges

[3182] The State's Natural Disaster Compensation Scheme is regulated through the Natural Disaster Compensation Act and the Natural Disaster Compensation Regulations, and is subordinate to the Ministry of Agriculture and Food

[3183] The scheme is administered by the Norwegian Directorate of Agriculture

[3184] Decisions can be appealed to the Complaints Board for Natural Disaster Cases

[3185] The State's Natural Disaster Compensation Scheme is financed by annual appropriations from the state budget

[3269] Fire and rescue services

[3270] The Government will ensure that municipalities have professional and effective fire and rescue services that carry out good fire prevention work and have a good ability to handle both everyday and larger and more demanding incidents

[3271] The fire and rescue service is the municipalities' most important technical rescue resource

[3272] There are currently 205 fire and rescue services with a total of approximately 12,000 employees, divided between approximately 4,000 full-time employees and 8,000 part-time employees

[3273] The fire and rescue service is present where people live and travel and provides rapid assistance when people need help, regardless of the time of day a fire or accident occurs

[3274] The breadth of missions handled by the fire and rescue service is large. As can be seen, an average of 46 people have died in fires each year over the past ten years

[3275] Over the past five years, an average of 36 people have died in fires each year

[3276] Fire statistics show that 90 percent of those who die in fires die in their homes

[3277] Three out of four people who die in fires belong to a risk group

[3278] Groups at risk include the elderly in need of assistance, drug addicts and people with mental health problems

[3279] To reduce the number of deaths in fires, it is necessary to focus efforts on reducing the risk and consequences of fires in homes, and to ensure the fire safety of risk groups in particular

[3280] Regulations on fire prevention, which came into force in 2016, have given municipal fire and rescue services greater freedom than before to use preventive resources where the need is greatest, and to implement targeted measures for the groups most exposed to fire

[3281] Feedback DSB has received from fire and rescue services indicates that the regulations have led to a strengthening of local fire prevention work, and that many municipalities are making a major local effort to ensure the fire safety of at-risk groups

[3282] Increased cooperation between the municipal health and care services and the fire and rescue service is a main strategy in the work to improve fire safety for groups at risk

[3283] In 2017, the Norwegian Directorate of Health and DSB published guidance for municipalities on such collaboration

[3284] Guidance work was strengthened in 2019 through the national initiative "Life-Critical

[3305] Education and competence development

[3306] The government will strengthen fire education by establishing a new education model for fire and rescue personnel that will replace the current agency school model

[3307] Today, fire and rescue personnel must be employed by a fire and rescue service and have completed in-house training before they can complete a formal course of education at the Norwegian Fire Academy

[3308] The state-owned model results in large differences in competence in the municipalities, and does not sufficiently safeguard the professional competence that the fire and rescue service needs

[3309] The new education model will consist of a public two-year vocational school for training fire and rescue personnel at the Norwegian Fire School in Tjeldsund municipality, and a higher education at bachelor's level for training leaders for the fire and rescue service

[3310] The establishment of a new vocational school has been initiated

[3311] New infrastructure is needed at the Norwegian Fire Academy before the vocational school can start up

[3312] The government proposes to allocate NOK 139.1 million in 2021 to begin construction of necessary infrastructure and further establish a new vocational school

[3317] When the new model is in place, part-time personnel will receive more uniform national training that is more in line with societal developments and the challenges of today and the future

[3319] The digital learning arena has been named "Branntavla" and is being developed with financial support from the Gjensidige Foundation and "The Great Fire Pledge

[3321] Role distribution between fire and rescue services, police and health services

[3322] General information about the emergency services' cooperation and efforts in each other's areas of responsibility The Government emphasizes good cooperation between the emergency services

[3323] Good cooperation between the fire and rescue services, the police and the health service is crucial for the tasks to be solved in the best possible way

[3324] Through each emergency service's statutory responsibility to provide assistance to citizens, there is a need for them to contribute to the task of other emergency services and other emergency response actors when necessary

[3325] In situations where it is required that multiple emergency services participate and cooperate, the police are the central actor for leading and coordinating the efforts of the emergency services

[3326] This is regulated both in the police's emergency planning system and in plans related to the rescue service

[3327] In general, it is felt that each emergency agency is fulfilling its primary responsibility and that the respective agencies' roles and responsibilities related to their core tasks are clarified and clear

[3328] Co-location of the emergency services' emergency call centres has contributed to better cooperation and information sharing between the emergency services during incidents, which in turn can lead to better utilisation of the emergency services' overall resources

[3329] In addition, triple alert procedures introduced in 2019 will improve the emergency services' shared situational understanding in missions that require coordination between agencies

[3330] In 2015, a joint national procedure was developed that describes how emergency personnel from fire, police and health can together save lives and limit damage in situations where ongoing life-threatening violence (PLIVO) is being perpetrated against multiple people

[3331] The procedure describes the pattern of action both when all three emergency services are present, and how emergency personnel from fire and health should assess situations where the police have not arrived

[3332] The assessment shall be carried out in consultation with the police operations center

[3333] The procedure is regularly trained with all three emergency services

[3334] Uniform routines and procedures ensure good and rapid handling of the most serious incidents, and promote even closer cooperation and a common understanding of the various emergency services' patterns of action

[3335] Separate collaboration meetings are also held between the agencies at both local and national levels, with attention to collaboration, joint development of disciplines and strengthened collaboration

[3336] The three emergency services have different organizations and locations, but all work according to the principle that life and health should be prioritized

[3337] This means that there will always be some assignments where the respective agencies initially carry out work within a 2020–2021 Report

[3338] Social security in an uncertain world is another agency's area of ​​responsibility

[3339] Basically, it is a strength for the country's preparedness that the emergency services can benefit from each other's different capacities in the event of incidents

[3340] If the first emergency service at an accident scene reports that the mission is not urgent for one or both of the other emergency services, it can also affect how the mission is prioritized against other simultaneous incidents

[3341] In all municipalities, there is interagency cooperation between the emergency services

[3342] After missions where cooperation between the emergency services has not functioned optimally, it is important to evaluate the events afterwards and follow up on learning points to ensure that the main responsibility of the individual emergency service is met

[3349] Fire and rescue services and police

[3350] The fire and rescue service is a municipal responsibility

[3351] The state governs the municipalities through laws and regulations, and the tasks of the fire and rescue service follow from the Fire and Explosion Protection Act

[3352] Each municipality must ensure the establishment and operation of a fire and rescue service that can carry out preventive and emergency preparedness tasks in accordance with the law in an efficient and safe manner, and carry out a risk and vulnerability analysis so that the fire and rescue service is best adapted to the tasks it may be faced with

[3353] It follows from the law that the head of the fire and rescue service (the fire chief) is in charge of firefighting, scene management in other accident situations until management is taken over by the police, and has authority to maintain order until the police arrive at the scene

[3354] According to the law, municipalities can assign other tasks to the fire and rescue service as long as this does not weaken the fire and rescue service's statutory tasks

[3355] It is up to the municipalities themselves to assess which other tasks the fire and rescue service has the capacity to perform

[3356] The statutory duties have not changed

[3357] The role and responsibility of the police are regulated by the Police Act and the core tasks have traditionally been linked to the police's security-creating activities, maintaining peace and order and combating crime

[3358] In enforcing these tasks, the police, as society's civilian power apparatus, have both the right and the duty to use force against citizens where this is necessary and proportionate

[3359] According to the Police Act, the police must fulfill their social mission, among other things, by being part of society's overall efforts to promote and strengthen citizens' legal certainty, security and general welfare in general

[3360] This requires that the police have close cooperation with, knowledge of and understanding of the responsibilities and roles of the other emergency services

[3361] There is generally close and good cooperation between the fire and rescue services and the police, and it is crucial for good preparedness and crisis management that the actors pay attention to cooperation

[3362] As a starting point, the tasks of the emergency services within the sectors are solved in line with line responsibility

[3363] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security has asked the Police Directorate and DSB to jointly look into the interaction between the two emergency services

[3364] This could form a basis for determining whether further follow-up is needed

[3414] More about forest fire preparedness The summer of 2018 was one of the most demanding forest fire seasons we have had in Norway, and showed how this can challenge preparedness

[3415] A prolonged drought and unusually heavy thunderstorms caused lightning to ignite a large number of fires throughout southern Norway

[3416] In addition to all the fires caused by lightning strikes, many fires started after burning grass, bonfires and barbecuing on disposable barbecues in nature. Responsibilities and resources in forest fire preparedness

[3417] Managing forest fires is a municipal responsibility

[3418] A number of cooperative arrangements on fire protection have been established between municipalities

[3419] The Fire and Explosion Protection Act requires municipalities to cooperate on the best possible utilization of resources, but it is up to each individual municipality to decide how extensive the cooperation should be

[3420] The state provides resources that reinforce this, such as the Civil Defense and forest fire helicopters

[3421] The state's forest fire helicopter is on permanent alert from April 15 to August 15 each year with contractual requirements for response time

[3422] The forest fire helicopter is normally stationed at Torp during the emergency period

[3423] If the forest fire danger is high in other parts of the country, the forest fire helicopter can be stationed at other bases

[3424] Today's agreement on forest fire helicopter preparedness is scalable

[3425] In the event of a major forest fire risk, DSB places several helicopters on standby, as long as there are helicopters available

[3426] In several counties, agreements have been made between municipalities and local flying clubs regarding monitoring forest fires with small aircraft

[3427] This is a very valuable addition to detecting forest fires at an early stage and preventing extensive damage, as well as a resource in management

[3428] DSB has the administrative responsibility for the scheme, while the Main Rescue Centre coordinates the actual use of the forest fire helicopters

[3429] The main rescue center issues a deployment order to forest fire helicopters based on a request for assistance from the local fire chief communicated through the 110 center

[3430] Mandatory leadership support is triggered when a fire chief is assigned assistance by forest fire helicopters

[3431] Leadership support has been established as a permanent duty arrangement with experienced fire chiefs nationwide

[3432] This means that senior fire officers with expertise assist fire chiefs in fires where forest fire helicopters are deployed

[3433] DSB administers the management support through Rogaland Fire and Rescue IKS

[3434] A total of 15–20 fire officers are included in the scheme, which means that there is one person on standby at all times during the same period as the helicopter standby from April 15 to August

[3435] Civil defense is an important reinforcement resource in the event of major forest fires

[3436] If necessary, the fire and rescue service's emergency manager will be able to request assistance from the civil defense district

[3437] The Civil Defence Staff in DSB can move personnel and equipment across civil defence district boundaries to where the need is greatest

[3438] In areas where there is a significant risk of forest fires, the fire chief, in consultation with the local forestry authorities, shall organize a special reserve force for operations in the event of such fires

[3439] Such reserve forces should be trained for current tasks

[3440] The Forest Fire Committee has worked since 1985 to increase the level of knowledge about forest fires and the fight against forest fires

[3441] The committee meets 2-3 times a year

[3442] The following organizations are represented on the committee

[3443] DSB, the Directorate of Agriculture, Skogbrand Forsikring, the Norwegian Fire Officers' Association, the Norwegian Air Sports Association (flight monitoring), the forestry industry organizations at the Norwegian Forest Owners' Association, the Norwegian Farmers' Association, MET, Helitrans AS (supplier of forest fire helicopters), the Norwegian Fire Protection Association, the Civil Defence, the Armed Forces and the Ministry of Agriculture and Food

[3444] The forum will, among other things, discuss roles and collaboration, and create a common understanding between actors

[3452] The Civil Defense is organized as part of DSB

[3453] Civil defense is part of total defense and has the primary task of protecting the civilian population in war, and is protected under the Geneva Convention

[3454] The Civil Defence is also a reinforcement resource that provides support to the emergency and preparedness agencies across the entire crisis spectrum

[3455] The Civil Defence Force consists of approximately 8,000 conscripts

[3456] The Civil Defence also operates a warning service, is part of the nuclear emergency response team and contributes during international disasters

[3457] The Civil Defence also has a preparedness and competence centre and a central warehouse at Starum in the Inland region

[3458] The Civil Defence's deployment statistics confirm that capacities and deliveries within reinforcement are relevant and in demand, and that the number of deployments is constantly increasing

[3459] The Civil Defence's efforts in 2020 have been largely linked to the corona-related situation, with a total of 60 corona-related efforts as of August 31, 2020, where 576 people have been involved for a total of 7,470 hours

[3460] The efforts have mainly consisted of assistance with tents for hospitals and emergency rooms in connection with sample collection, as well as assistance with improvised cleaning sites for, among others, the ambulance service, the police and rescue helicopters

[3461] In addition, the Civil Defence has assisted with information to residents, guarding and security, and material assistance, etc. The Civil Defence's crews and material constitute a critical resource in the event of long-term and simultaneous incidents

[3462] In connection with the revised national budget 2020, the allocation to the Civil Defence has been increased by NOK 30 million for training, basic courses, personnel, equipment and maintenance in the Civil Defence

[3463] The Civil Defense is divided into 20 districts, each led by a district commander

[3464] The Civil Defence's district structure may appear somewhat inappropriate in light of recent changes among actors with whom the Civil Defence collaborates

[3465] Any changes in the district structure must be seen in the context of the needs that such collaboration requires

[3466] However, the government has decided not to prioritize changing the district structure of the Civil Defence at this time

[3467] Future needs for civil protection measures

[3468] Today's concept of civil protection has four main elements: – warning the population – evacuation of the civilian population in war or when war threatens – shelters – self-protection/self-preparedness

[3469] In the Civil Protection Act, the Civil Defence is given overall responsibility for civil protection measures, but several actors, including the police and local authorities, are responsible for individual elements

[3470] Today's civil protection concept was established as a result of experiences during World War II and developments during the Cold War

[3471] The measures are typically geared towards the threats and types of weapons of the time

[3472] However, the risk and vulnerability picture has changed significantly in recent years

[3473] Changes such as new complex threats increase the need for notification and correct information from the authorities

[3474] What society should protect itself against in a digitalized world is also crucial in assessing civil protection measures

[3475] DSB – with assistance from, among others, the Defence Research Institute (FFI) – has, on behalf of the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, prepared a concept study with recommendations on which civil defence and civil protection measures

[3476] Norway should have in the future

[3477] The report was sent for broad consultation

[3478] In June 2019, DSB submitted an impact and cost analysis of the recommendations for a future civil protection concept

[3479] In summary, the civil protection measures are overall inadequate and outdated, and the measures will not be able to protect the population in a satisfactory manner

[3480] There is therefore a need to make adjustments that make society better equipped to withstand current and future threats

[3481] Societal security in an uncertain world Design of future civil protection measures

[3482] The government has decided that the design of future civil protection measures will be based on three main measures: timely population warning with a high degree of coverage, appropriate evacuation to safe places and self-preparedness

[3483] Timely and accurate population warning with a high coverage rate for peace, crisis and war is crucial

[3484] The Norwegian Civil Defence's typhoon system is currently our only national system for population warning and consists of 1,244 operational warning systems

[3485] These reach about half the population, that is, those living in cities and densely populated areas where siren systems were deployed during the Cold War

[3486] The warning system was primarily built to warn the population of impending air attacks

[3487] It is appropriate to have a supplementary, national warning system where precise and timely notification of unwanted, potentially dangerous events is possible

[3488] The Storting therefore agreed with the government's proposal to allocate NOK 1.1 million to DSB in the 2020 state budget to investigate a system for mobile-based population notification

[3489] Evacuation to safe places

[3490] It is the police's responsibility to evacuate

[3491] This involves deciding on appropriate evacuation and ensuring that affected people reach safety in crisis situations

[3492] The municipality's task is to ensure that the basic needs of the evacuees are met

[3493] Furthermore, in line with the municipal emergency preparedness obligation, municipalities are required to prepare an overall emergency preparedness plan (see section 10.4.1), which must contain an evacuation plan

[3494] Municipal emergency plans are usually generic in form, and there is a need to assess the planning system, especially in municipalities with strategically important areas

[3495] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security will therefore assign DSB to assess the municipal evacuation planning system and to guide municipalities in strategically important areas to ensure that they have an up-to-date plan

[3496] This plan must be developed in collaboration with relevant stakeholders such as the police, the Armed Forces, county governors and municipalities

[3504] Shelters as a civil protection measure are regulated in the Civil Protection Act and associated regulations

[3505] Norway currently has just under 20,000 shelters with space for approximately 2.5 million people

[3506] These are divided into approximately 600 public shelters with space for approximately 300,000 people and approximately 19,200 private shelters with approximately 2.2 million places

[3507] The evacuation shelters have a coverage rate of about 50 percent of the population, but there are large regional differences nationwide

[3508] The coverage rate reflects the assessment of the threat landscape at the time

[3509] According to current regulations, shelters must provide good protection against the effects of conventional weapons, radioactive fallout, biological and chemical warfare agents

[3510] The requirements for protection are higher for public shelters than for private ones

[3511] Regulations on shelters require that the rooms can be prepared within 72 hours and that people can stay there for up to six hours

[3512] Conditions that affect the length of stay are particularly air quality and access to drinking water

[3513] The owner of the shelter is responsible for fulfilling the requirements of the regulations

[3514] The Civil Defence carries out condition checks on the shelters and processes applications for exemption from current regulations

[3515] A number of shelters are used on a daily basis for other purposes, including by voluntary organizations, sports teams and others

[3516] Changes in the security policy situation after the Cold War led, among other things, to the Storting, when considering Report to the Storting

[3517] No. 25 (1997–98) Main guidelines for civil emergency preparedness activities and development in the period 1999–

[3518] St. no. 241 (1997–98), agreed to a temporary halt in the construction of new shelters pending a new protection concept

[3519] This is still the current practice, which has resulted in the coverage of shelters constantly decreasing as a result of population growth and the removal of poorly maintained shelters

[3520] FFI believes that shelters have lost much of their relevance in light of a changed risk and vulnerability picture, new vulnerabilities in society and new weapons technology

[3521] A public emergency committee (NOU

[3522] When it really matters) also considered today's shelters as neither relevant nor adapted to society's challenges and threat picture

[3523] The committee pointed out that socio-economic and emergency preparedness considerations indicate that such facilities should be decommissioned and that resources should be directed towards prevention and management of vulnerability described in the national risk picture

[3524] The population will probably not have time to seek cover in a shelter, as many of the rooms are located incorrectly with respect to where the population is actually staying today

[3525] Several NATO countries consider shelters to be less relevant due to the short warning time in the event of an attack, and recommend that civil protection be based to a greater extent on effective warning and information, and that cover must be sought where one is

[3526] According to the government's assessment, the current shelter solution is outdated

[3527] However, there is a need for safe places to stay for the population throughout the crisis spectrum, if evacuation is necessary

[3528] The Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness will assign DSB, in collaboration with relevant actors, to assess and propose criteria for safe places for the population to stay during evacuation across the entire crisis spectrum

[3529] As part of this work, special consideration will be given to continuing to provide shelters with high protection capabilities in particularly vulnerable areas

[3530] The shelter scheme in its current form will be discontinued when a new scheme for safe places of residence has been established for the population across the entire crisis spectrum

[3531] Self-preparedness In the fall of 2018, DSB launched a self-preparedness campaign to help the population prepare for a crisis, including the ability to take care of themselves and those around them for at least three days in the event of incidents and crises affecting critical infrastructure

[3532] A brochure with advice on self-preparedness was distributed to all households in the country

[3533] The campaign has received considerable attention and has contributed to increased awareness among the population about the importance of personal preparedness

[3534] Self-protection measures provide good protection against many types of undesirable events both in peacetime and against acts of war

[3554] Management of the electrical safety area

[3555] Electrification is an important part of the green shift, but it also entails new load patterns on the power grid and new types of installations

[3556] When lighting and heating are controlled wirelessly, the line between electrical safety and e-commerce is blurred

[3557] When electrical energy is produced at consumers' premises, the line between electrical safety and energy production is blurred

[3558] In smart cities and with the “internet of things”, many services are connected online, which increases vulnerability and dependence on the internet to operate lighting and heating and the risk of hacking of electricity management

[3559] Technological developments are changing the boundaries with other administrative and government areas

[3560] Today's management model provides many interfaces

[3561] DSB administers the Act on Supervision of Electrical Installations and Electrical Equipment (the Electricity Supervision Act), the National Communications Authority (Nkom) administers the Act on Electronic Communications (the ecom act) and the NVE administers the Energy Act

[3562] In recent years, DSB has pointed out several challenges with the current management model

[3563] Fire statistics show that fires are less likely to be caused by faults in electrical installations, and more likely to be caused by incorrect use in at risk groups and faults in electrical products

[3564] Future electrical safety challenges are largely linked to the use of new technology and services

[3565] There is a need to look more closely at how electricity security can best be ensured in the green transition, including possible division of responsibility among the responsible sector authorities

[3566] Increased use of electricity, more public authorities with responsibility and private-public collaboration give reason to assess whether the current management model in the area of electrical safety is appropriate

[3567] Challenges in the area of electrical safety are complex and cross-sectoral

[3568] The Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness, the Ministry of Local Government and Modernisation, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries and the Ministry of Petroleum and Energy will establish a working group to put forward proposals for a comprehensive and cost-effective management of the electricity safety area

[3569] The group will have participation from DSB, NKOM, NVE and the Norwegian Maritime Directorate

[3570] The business community will also be involved, for example through a reference group

[3571] The purpose of the review shall be a comprehensive and cost-effective management of the electrical safety area

[3575] For example, when a natural- Meld

[3606] DLE shall have a risk-based approach to its inspections, and shall have a particular focus on groups at risk

[3607] Through its inspection activities, DLE helps reduce the number of fires caused by electricity

[3649] Storage of explosives In August 2020, Beirut was hit by a massive explosion in a warehouse containing large quantities of ammonium nitrate

[3650] This led to extensive damage throughout the capital

[3651] About 190 people died and more than 6,000 were injured

[3652] The Lebanese government has estimated that the explosions have left more than 300,000 people homeless

[3653] In Norway, ammonium nitrate is mainly used in fertilizer and for the production of explosives

[3654] Ammonium nitrate is a so-called starting material for explosives, and in recent years strict requirements have also been imposed on the security of the substance to prevent it from being misappropriated and misused

[3655] It is a chemical substance with properties that indicate that regulation of the substance is necessary for reasons of public safety

[3656] In Norway, there are a number of requirements for dangerous substances such as ammonium nitrate

[3657] To prevent unwanted incidents when storing this substance, there are requirements for risk assessments and competence requirements for people who handle the substance

[3658] Furthermore, there are requirements for proper storage and assessment of space limitations during storage

[3659] When storing above certain quantities, there is also a reporting obligation to DSB

[3660] Special requirements apply to the storage of ammonium nitrate used in the production of explosives

[3661] In Norway, all warehouses with more than 50 tons of ammonium nitrate are subject to supervision by DSB

[3662] Such warehouses are also covered by the Major Accident Regulations and are closely monitored

[3663] Warehouses under 50 tons are subject to supervision by the fire and rescue service

[3666] Societal security in an uncertain world Prevention, emergency preparedness and rescue services in our northern sea areas

[3667] Norway is a maritime nation

[3668] We have an ocean area that is several times larger than our land area

[3669] Including islands, islets and fjords, Norway has one of the world's longest coastlines

[3670] A significant portion of the Norwegian economy is linked to the sea

[3671] Oil and gas, shipping, tourism, and the fishing and seafood industry are important industries that create employment throughout the country, and especially along the coast

[3672] Large parts of the Norwegian sea areas lie north of the Arctic Circle

[3673] Most of the total shipping in the entire Arctic today goes through Norwegian waters

[3674] Ship traffic has increased in recent years

[3675] Growth is expected to continue

[3676] Melting sea ice and warmer seas have led to greater activity

[3677] The fishing fleet is moving further north, cruise traffic in polar areas is growing, and new shipping routes are being considered as the ice melts

[3678] Increased maritime activity brings a greater risk of accidents

[3679] Norway has long placed emphasis on a presence in the maritime areas of the North to assert sovereignty and sovereign rights, safeguard the exercise of authority and contribute to predictability and stability

[3680] This is an important part of the government's overall High North policy

[3681] As a coastal and flag state, Norway has a responsibility to facilitate safe shipping traffic in vulnerable areas in the Arctic

[3682] Norway is a leading rescue and emergency response actor in the northern sea areas

[3683] We have a unique publicly organized rescue service that works well, and trust in the service is high

[3684] At the same time, emergency preparedness in these remote and weather-prone areas is demanding, and raises questions about what requirements can be placed on the individual actor's responsibility for their own safety

[3685] What each individual does for their own safety and preparedness will always be important

[3686] At sea, it is absolutely crucial

[3687] Those operating in these waters must be aware that the climate, distances and time factor will make certain rescue operations very demanding, no matter how many resources the rescue service has

[3688] It must be a prerequisite that actors themselves implement measures to prevent and handle any accidents

[3689] There is considerable responsibility on the part of the individual skipper, shipowner and operator

[3690] This chapter explains the challenges Norway faces when it comes to emergency preparedness and rescue services in northern sea areas, what resources are available and what the government is doing

[3691] Government policy

[3692] – Improve emergency communications in northern waters through expanded high-frequency radio coverage (HF) and listening watch from coastal radio stations on HF

[3693] – Establish broadband capacity for both civilian and military users in the Arctic from

[3694] – Phase in the new rescue helicopters that will significantly strengthen rescue preparedness. – Aim to establish a new base in Tromsø that will contribute to increased rescue helicopter capacity in the north. – Strengthen Arctic maritime expertise by establishing an Arctic maritime competence node

[3695] – Assess current and future maritime safety and emergency preparedness challenges related to cruise traffic in Norwegian waters and adjacent sea areas

[3696] The government has appointed a committee to discuss the challenges and propose measures in this area

[3697] – Investigate how the maritime emergency and safety service (coastal radio service) should be structured in the future

[3698] – Further develop cooperation on common challenges in the Arctic within rescue and emergency preparedness through agreements related to international rescue cooperation in northern sea areas

[3699] Responsibility for search and rescue in northern sea areas Norway's obligations for sea and air rescue services are enshrined in a number of international conventions

[3700] St. 5 2020–2021 Social security in an uncertain world tions and agreements

[3701] The framework for the rescue service is set out in the International Convention on Maritime Search and Rescue of 1979 (SAR Convention), the Convention on International Civil Aviation of 1944 (ICAO Convention) and the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea of 1974 (SOLAS Convention

[3702] The 1982 UN Convention on the Law of the Sea also provides a framework for states' rights, freedom of action and duties at sea, and, among other things, obliges the flag state to require the master to provide assistance

[3703] The convention obligations are operationalized through a joint international plan, the so-called IAMSAR manual (International Aeronautical and Maritime Search and Rescue Manual

[3704] Norway's geographical area of responsibility for the rescue service is, in addition to Norwegian territory, the sea and ocean areas and the airspace above which are determined at any time by Norway in consultation with neighboring states on the basis of international agreements where Norway has committed to providing rescue services

[3705] In practice, this means very large areas of sea in the north

[3706] As a result of Norway becoming a party to an agreement on search and rescue in the Arctic in 2011, the rescue area of responsibility was expanded so that Norway has responsibility further east towards the Russian area of responsibility than previously, as well as north of Svalbard and all the way up to the pole point (see Figure 11.1 and Section

[3707] The Norwegian rescue service is administratively coordinated by the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, and it is the ministry that provides detailed instructions, mandate and guidelines for the performance of the rescue service

[3708] The sea and air rescue service is always managed and coordinated directly from the Main Rescue Centre, either from the Southern Norway department (HRS SN) or from the Northern Norway department (HRS NN

[3709] The coordination of incidents on land is in most cases delegated to one of the local rescue centres, following instructions from the Main Rescue Centre

[3711] The change came into effect on February

[3714] The additional function of the police chiefs as leaders of the rescue teams at the Central Rescue Centre will continue as it is today

[3715] HRS SN is located near Stavanger Airport Sola

[3716] The center's area of responsibility extends from the Skagerrak up to 65 degrees north

[3717] In the south, HRS SN's area of ​​responsibility borders Sweden and Denmark, and in the west, the United Kingdom

[3718] The central office also has overall responsibility for all rescue services on land from Trøndelag and southward

[3719] HRS NN is located in Bodø

[3724] The main rescue center has local rescue centers

[3727] Local rescue centers are primarily used to coordinate and coordinate rescue operations on land, not at sea

[3741] Social security in an uncertain world

[3742] Challenges in northern sea areas

[3743] Icing and cold expose vessels to heavy loads on the hull and machinery

[3744] Polar low pressure systems, which form in winter when cold, Arctic air flows out over the open ocean, occur at short notice and produce intense thunderstorms with strong winds and snow showers

[3745] Strong winds, high waves and fog are common in northern sea areas

[3746] Forecasting weather in the Arctic is more challenging than further south

[3747] The rapid climate change in the area poses an additional challenge

[3748] The warming in the Arctic is more than twice the global average

[3749] The extent of sea ice varies greatly from year to year, but the long-term trend is clearly downward

[3750] In the central Arctic Ocean, sea ice has decreased by 65 percent during the period

[3751] As sea ice becomes thinner and less widespread, it also becomes more mobile

[3808] Preventive maritime safety To prevent accidents and harmful emissions, it is important that shipping operates with high safety and environmental standards

[3809] Special conditions prevail in the highlands, and it is important that the regulations are adapted to this

[3810] Much has been done in the last ten years to increase maritime safety in the North

[3811] The most important thing is the work to prevent accidents

[3812] The government is working nationally and internationally to ensure that vessels and equipment are suitable for operation in polar waters and that the crew has the necessary expertise

[3813] In addition, there is work on traffic monitoring and control of traffic through Norwegian waters

[3814] As with other waters, shipping in the Arctic is covered by international regulations, including ship standards and crew qualifications, set by the United Nations Maritime Organization

[3815] IMO (International Maritime Organisation

[3816] It is important to ensure that ships are built and equipped according to the conditions in which they will operate, that the captain and crew are trained to handle the challenges they may encounter, and that the ship is operated accordingly

[3817] IMO's work on the Polar Code is an important effort that has been made to ensure sustainable development in shipping in the North

[3818] The Polar Code is divided into two parts, a safety section that applies to technical standards for ships, qualifications for crews and operations in polar regions, and an environmental section that is intended to help prevent pollution

[3819] It is crucial for the shipping company to analyze the operating area for the ship, so that any operational restrictions for the ship correspond to the conditions prevailing in the operating area

[3820] The polar ship certificate and operations manual must reflect this and any operational limitations

[3821] The Polar Code will help reduce the likelihood of unwanted incidents, including increasing the safety of ships and crews, and protecting the vulnerable environment in these areas

[3822] Svalbard lies within the geographical entry point for the Polar Code

[3823] The goal is to reduce the risk of adverse incidents during maritime transport in Svalbard, so that damage to life, health and safety is reduced. VHF stands for very high frequency, MF for medium frequency and HF for high frequency

[3847] Regulations on the construction, equipment and operation of passenger ships in the territorial waters of Svalbard, which were issued by the Norwegian Maritime Authority, entered into force on 1 January

[3848] The regulations stipulate that passenger ships in the territorial waters of Svalbard must have SOLAS standards including

[3849] This means that passenger ships sailing in the waters around Svalbard have been given requirements that are adapted to the unique conditions in the polar region

[4062] GMDSS sets requirements for equipment on ships and provides guidelines for how individual member states should build their systems for emergency communications

[4063] GMDSS consists of equipment on board ships, equipment on land, and satellites

[4074] Study on emergency preparedness challenges with increasing cruise traffic

[4075] Norway is a unique coastal state that is well suited for cruise traffic

[4076] Archipelago, fjords, northern lights, midnight sun and an Arctic climate in the north make us attractive

[4077] The cruise industry provides income and jobs, and tourists get to experience beautiful nature

[4078] At the same time, we have a demanding and weather-hardened coast

[4079] Climatic conditions, long distances and darkness present special challenges the further north we go

[4080] The rescue operation at Hustadvika with “Viking Sky” on March 23, 2019 showed how serious it can be when an engine failure occurs on a cruise ship close to land, in strong onshore winds and rough seas

[4081] The incident was close to having catastrophic consequences

[4082] In this very demanding situation, the Southern Norway Main Rescue Centre coordinated the rescue operation, where resources from, among others

[4083] The Coast Guard, the rescue helicopter service, helicopters from the petroleum industry and privately owned tugboats assisted in the operation at sea and in the air

[4084] On land, police, health personnel, municipalities, the Civil Defense, volunteers, the Home Guard and other emergency resources played important roles

[4085] It turned out that the cooperation between the various rescue actors worked well

[4086] The Directorate for Civil Protection and Emergency Preparedness also concluded in its evaluation report that there had been a successful rescue operation and good handling of the evacuees on land

[4087] The Government has appointed a public committee to assess maritime safety and emergency preparedness challenges related to cruise traffic in Norwegian waters and adjacent sea areas

[4088] The committee will provide a description of current cruise traffic, as well as outline future developments

[4089] Based on such a survey, the committee will discuss the emergency preparedness challenges that cruise traffic brings with it

[4090] This involves mapping the ability to coordinate and handle serious incidents with cruise ships, including handling evacuated people

[4091] The committee will propose measures on how the cruise industry itself can contribute to maintaining, improving and dimensioning its own preparedness

[4092] This will involve an assessment of risk and risk-reducing measures, such as weather and seasonal restrictions, navigational guidelines, passenger restrictions and other emergency measures

[4093] Furthermore, the committee shall emphasize preventive measures that are practically, organizationally and legally possible to implement

[4094] The committee will discuss which objectives ensure an adequate level of preparedness, and make recommendations on which measures can be considered to achieve these objectives

[4095] The committee will familiarize itself with how other Arctic coastal states are developing preventive measures and what adjustments are being made to handle increasing cruise traffic

[4096] The committee will assess the opportunities for learning and transfer of experience to Norwegian conditions

[4097] In its work, the committee shall consider Norway's responsibility and role in international and regional cooperation on search and rescue

[4099] The purpose is to contribute to ensuring that Norwegian marine and coastal areas are used and managed in an efficient, sustainable and well-coordinated manner

[4109] International rescue cooperation in northern sea areas With large sea areas, scattered resources and long distances, it is important to have rescue and emergency preparedness agreements with our neighboring countries in the north

[4110] The nearest rescue resource can often be located in another country, and good cooperation is necessary to make the best possible use of the combined resources in the region

[4111] The Arctic Council is the only political cooperation body between the eight Arctic states at the government level

[4112] The Agreement on Search and Rescue in the Arctic was the first legally binding agreement negotiated within the framework of the Arctic Council

[4113] The agreement was signed in 2011 between the member countries Canada, Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Russia, Sweden and the United States

[4114] The agreement came into effect in January

[4115] Through the agreement, the Arctic is divided into regions of responsibility for search and rescue, and national contact points have been established for the exchange of information and mutual aid and assistance

[4116] HRS is the operational contact point for Norway, and the Ministry of Justice and Public Security is the so-called "competent authority" according to the agreement

[4117] HRS NN also participates in the expert group for follow-up of the search and rescue agreement under the Arctic Council's Emergency Prevention, Preparedness and Response (EPPR) working group

[4118] Several exercises have been arranged in connection with this agreement

[4119] For example, mass rescue from cruise ships off the coast of Alaska was a scenario during an exercise

[4120] Through the search and rescue agreement, binding cooperation on rescue services in the Arctic has been established

[4121] Norway wants to further develop

[4122] The Arctic Council's ability and capacity to promote cooperation on common challenges in the Arctic

[4123] Norway is also party to a bilateral maritime rescue agreement with Russia

[4124] The agreement originally dates from 1957, but was later replaced by a more comprehensive agreement in 1988, which was again revised

[4125] HRS and the Murmansk Maritime Rescue Centre (MRCC Murmansk) have conducted the annual sea rescue exercise "Exercise Barents" in the outer Varangerfjord in the border area between Norway and Russia since

[4126] The objective of the exercise is to practice the agreement itself with a practical event where resources from the Russian Northern Fleet and the Russian Coast Guard participate together with, among others, the Norwegian Coast Guard, 330 Squadron and the Norwegian Rescue Society

[4127] Since 2006, the Norwegian Coastal Administration and their Russian partner have linked up with the rescue exercise to conduct a subsequent oil spill response exercise on the same day as the sea rescue exercise

[4128] Responsibility for planning and implementation alternates every two years, and in 2020, HRS NN was to arrange the exercise

[4129] However, the exercise was canceled due to the corona situation

[4142] Societal security in an uncertain world Box 11.7 ARCSAR – increased expertise for better preparedness in the North

[4143] The Northern Norway Rescue Centre (HRS NN) has received 35 million kroner in grants over a 5-year period through the EU program HORIZON 2020 for the project ARCSAR – search and rescue, and oil spill response in Arctic waters

[4144] ARCSAR started up

[4145] The project's main goal is to establish an international network consisting of representatives from authorities, academia, organizations and emergency personnel to better meet challenges related to security and risk threats in the Arctic and North Atlantic region, including cruise traffic and the oil and gas industry

[4146] HRS NN leads ARCSAR, which has 21 partners from a total of 13 countries; Iceland, Faroe Islands, Great Britain, Ireland, Italy, USA, Russia, Germany, Finland, Sweden, New Zealand, Canada and Norway

[4147] ARCSAR aims to: – establish and support a new Arctic and North Atlantic network in security and emergency preparedness – contribute to increased understanding of priority areas of effort in security and emergency relief – closely monitor developments in innovation and research in, among other things, security systems, disaster risk and crisis management – identify critical obstacles and deficiencies in capacity, expertise and infrastructure – uncover common arenas and opportunities for increased collaboration in emergency situations – stimulate partners to provide sufficient resources in the event of incidents – communicate the results of the project and activity improvements to relevant end users

[4148] Among the Norwegian partners in the project are the Norwegian Coastal Administration, the Coast Guard, the Norwegian Meteorological Institute

[4149] the shipping association Maritimt Forum Nord and Nord University

[4153] Further development of work on societal security The Government has strengthened work on societal security in several areas since the previous societal security report, Report

[4154] St. 10 (2016–2017) Risk in a safe society, cf

[4155] S (2016–2017), was presented

[4156] The legal basis for societal security work has been further developed, and our prerequisites for having knowledge and an overview of risks and vulnerabilities have been strengthened

[4157] This chapter describes completed and ongoing measures that contribute to further developing work on social security, as well as the government's further work within the areas discussed

[4158] Government policy

[4159] The government will: – Based on the ministries' status and condition assessments, assess our ability to ensure continuity in critical societal functions

[4160] – Evaluate the system of status and condition assessments for critical societal functions

[4161] – Conduct supervision based on further developed supervision schemes in accordance with the Public Safety Instructions and the new Safety Act, respectively

[4162] – Further develop DSB's analyses of crisis scenarios

[4163] – Strengthen the basis for planning, implementation, evaluation and follow-up of exercises

[4164] – Review and revise the framework of the 14 critical societal functions, in light of experiences from the corona pandemic, also with regard to the Security Act and basic national functions

[4165] – Process the recommendations of the Emergency Authorization Committee

[4166] A better legal basis for work on societal security

[4167] The work on societal security deals with a challenge that is constantly changing

[4168] The Government has further developed the legal basis for work on social security

[4169] The legal basis defines and distributes responsibilities and roles between different actors

[4170] This is a prerequisite for effective and purposeful social security work

[4171] New knowledge about the status and condition of societal security The societal security instruction places special requirements on ministries with primary responsibility for critical societal functions (see Table

[4172] One of the requirements is that ministries with primary responsibility must have an overview of the condition within their own area of responsibility, including by preparing status and condition assessments for the critical societal functions for which they have primary responsibility

[4173] This involves an assessment of the ability of society to maintain its functions if exposed to various stresses

[4174] By the end of 2020, all planned status and condition assessments will have been completed

[4175] Based on these condition assessments, the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness will establish a comprehensive overview of the status and condition of our ability to maintain continuity in critical societal functions

[4176] In addition, the scheme is evaluated with status and condition assessments

[4177] Important questions in the evaluation are whether the scheme meets its objectives and what the effects are

[4259] Further development of DSB's analyses of crisis scenarios Since 2011, the Directorate for Civil Protection and Emergency Preparedness (DSB) has prepared risk analyses of serious incidents that could affect Norway and that we must be prepared to handle

[4260] The work is being carried out on behalf of the Ministry of Justice and Public Security

[4261] The risk analyses are based on a broad risk picture (all hazard approach) that includes natural events, major accidents and intentional acts

[4262] Analyses of crisis scenarios provide input for risk analyses and emergency planning at departments, subordinate agencies, county governors and municipalities

[4263] The work on the analyses crosses sectors and involves a wide range of public and private actors

[4264] The risk analyses are part of the national knowledge and planning basis for work on societal safety

[4265] In 2019, DSB published a comprehensive report presenting all 25 risk analyses produced to date (see box

[4266] The new report presents short versions of all 25 risk analyses, including six new analyses produced since the previous comprehensive report

[4267] Several of the analyses have also been presented previously in more comprehensive reports with a more detailed knowledge base

[4268] All analyses are available on DSB's website

[4269] Two of the crisis scenarios are particularly relevant in connection with the corona pandemic, the pandemic and drug shortage scenarios, respectively (see also Chapter

[4270] These are also the scenarios that DSB has assessed as having the highest risk

[4271] The Directorate has, in continuation of DSB's report, reviewed the drug preparedness and proposed a number of measures

[4272] The crisis scenarios are not dimensioning the preparedness, as, for example, the dimensioning of the Figure 12.1 Analyses of crisis scenarios

[4276] In 2019, DSB conducted an evaluation of the crisis scenarios on behalf of the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness

[4340] The Emergency Powers Committee was appointed on 9 February 2018 to assess whether, outside of the cases regulated by the Emergency Powers Act, a cross-sectoral authorization provision should be introduced that gives the government the authority to temporarily supplement, and if necessary, make exceptions to, current legislation

[4341] The committee was also asked to consider whether, in addition to this, a legal basis should be drawn up to temporarily suspend individuals' statutory rights, or possibly modify how the rights must be fulfilled

[4342] The committee submitted its report to NOU

[4343] When the crisis strikes on June

[4344] The committee has concluded that the advantages of an emergency powers act outweigh the disadvantages, provided that the use of the power is subject to a number of substantive and procedural conditions

[4345] The committee has proposed a legal basis that, in extraordinary crises, allows temporary regulations to be issued that complement, supplement or deviate from legislation, if the situation cannot be handled within the framework of applicable legislation and there is a danger of delay

[4346] The regulations cannot go further than what is necessary to handle the crisis, and they cannot deviate from rules in the Constitution or in conventions that, according to the Human Rights Act, apply as Norwegian law

[4347] Furthermore, the committee proposes the following procedural guarantees of legal certainty: – The regulation must be issued by the King in Council. – The regulation and the justification for it must be presented to the Storting within ten days

[4348] – The Storting may repeal the regulations at any time by at least 1/3 of the votes

[4349] – The regulations can be valid for a maximum of six months

[4350] The committee's proposal was sent for consultation with a consultation deadline of December

[4351] The Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness is now considering the committee's recommendations

[4352] The Ministry's assessment will also draw on the experiences gained in connection with the virus outbreak, see section

[4491] EU Civil Emergency Response Mechanism Norway participates in the EU Civil Emergency Response Mechanism

[4492] The purpose of the scheme is to facilitate broad cooperation in Europe within civil security and emergency preparedness, and is the most important instrument in the EEA area for civil disaster response and for other civil security and emergency preparedness work

[4493] For Norway, the scheme represents an important safety net

[4494] In the event of an incident occurring in Norway that exceeds national capacities, Norwegian authorities may request assistance from the EU

[4495] Norway has benefited from the scheme in connection with handling the corona pandemic

[4496] Participation in the scheme has been particularly valuable in relation to the

[4497] St. 5 2020–2021 Social security in an uncertain world participation in the work of repatriating Norwegian citizens, but also as a political entrance to a number of meeting arenas

[4499] Norway can also provide assistance to other countries through this cooperation, and Norway makes the Norwegian Emergency Medical Team (NOR EMT) available, among other things

[4504] EU cooperation in this field is continuously developing, and in March 2019 the EU adopted changes to the scheme

[4505] The most important changes are a strengthening of the civil emergency reserve, the creation of rescEU, and a strengthening of preventive work in the participating states

[4506] The civil emergency reserve is a reserve of resources in the form of response capacities and modules, emergency resources and experts, which are intended to be able to assist other states in the event of a crisis

[4507] The Norwegian Emergency Medical Team is part of this reserve, currently as a pilot

[4508] The change in 2019 partly involves simplifications in the use of the emergency reserve, and the fact that the available capacities will be able to receive a higher degree of cost coverage for adaptation, repair and operational operations

[4509] rescEU is an additional reserve of resources that can be used in crises in the Member States when national capacities and the civil emergency reserve are insufficient

[4510] Examples of which resources should be in rescEU are forest fire helicopters, forest fire planes and air ambulances for highly infectious patients

[4511] In addition to strengthening the civil emergency reserve and the creation of rescEU, prevention has been given a central place

[4512] The amendment decision specifies that the prevention area needs further efforts, where key measures are the further development of national and regional risk assessments, risk management capabilities, and planning and management of risk

[4513] In June 2019, the Storting approved the inclusion of the changes in the EU's civil preparedness regime in the EEA Agreement, and the changes therefore also apply to Norway. Germany holds the EU presidency in the autumn of 2020, and has made crisis management a priority

[4514] It is likely that the scheme will be further developed as a result of experience from handling the corona pandemic
