[4532] Nordic cooperation

[4533] Nordic cooperation in the field of public security is characterised by close dialogue on issues related to Nordic security, the Nordic region's immediate surroundings and European and global issues

[4534] The countries often share assessments of common challenges and how they should be handled, and extensive cooperation is underway to strengthen societal security

[4535] The Nordic countries have a common desire to contribute to NATO, the EU, the UN and our neighboring regions

[4536] Through the Haga cooperation, which is a politically initiated cooperation on societal security from 2009, it is being facilitated that the Nordic countries have coordinated positions to the greatest possible extent to influence these organizations

[4537] Increasingly closer and more extensive work within the EU's civil preparedness scheme is facilitating the strengthening of Nordic cooperation by drawing on EU support and funding schemes

[4538] The Nordic Haga cooperation is in continuous development

[4539] The common overall goal is to strengthen the Nordic countries' ability to prevent and reduce the consequences of major accidents, natural and man-made disasters, and other societal crises within the emergency preparedness area

[4540] The work is in accordance with the Nordic Declaration of Solidarity

[4541] Norway held the presidency in The Hague

[4542] Against the background of a new and changed threat landscape and climate change that contributes to more extreme weather in the Nordic region, the Nordic ministers agreed in the Oslo conclusions 2019 to further develop cooperation in the following three areas

[4543] Nordic forest fire/wildfire

[4544] cooperation, Nordic cooperation on CBRN and Nordic cooperation on emergency communications

[4545] In addition to the three areas mentioned above, the Nordic ministers agreed to focus on a number of other future areas that are important for emergency preparedness work in general, and that will be relevant to include in ongoing work, also when it comes to sharing knowledge and experiences within the Haga cooperation

[4546] This applies specifically to civil-military cooperation, hybrid activities and the importance of the High North

[4547] The annual report to the Storting on Nordic cooperation highlights the Haga cooperation, the Oslo conclusions 2019 and the development plan for Haga cooperation 2019–

[4548] The Haga collaboration was politically initiated

[4549] In a meeting between the Nordic ministers responsible for civil security and emergency preparedness, the declaration from the meeting, the Haga I Declaration, stated that the Nordic countries should jointly examine and specify work in various areas within civil security

[4550] In 2013, a new platform for Nordic cooperation in the field of civil security was established, the Haga II Declaration, where the goal is a robust Nordic region through, among other things, prevention, handling and recovery from serious incidents

[4551] It is also a goal to achieve a Nordic region “without borders”, to avoid bureaucratic and practical obstacles to cross-border cooperation

[4552] Follow-up to Haga II stems from the conclusions of the regular meetings of the Nordic ministers responsible for public security

[4553] In 2016, Norway and Sweden became the first two countries in the world to interconnect their national emergency networks, Nødnett and Rakel, respectively

[4554] Recently, Finland and Sweden and Finland and Norway have also established similar bilateral solutions

[4555] This has provided emergency and preparedness actors with efficient and secure communication across national borders and during operations in neighboring countries

[4556] The three-way interconnection (Finland-Norway-Sweden) was launched in the autumn

[4557] This provides smoother communication when working on regional challenges, and makes it even easier to help each other prevent crime and handle incidents

[4558] In addition to joint speaking groups, common guidelines and routines, as well as knowledge of each other's emergency management and methods, will contribute to making it easier, safer and more effective to work across national and organizational borders

[4559] There is agreement between the countries that future solutions must facilitate emergency communication throughout the Nordic region and with other international actors

[4560] Societal security in an uncertain world Nordic defense cooperation In recent years, the Nordic countries have strengthened their defense cooperation and expanded cooperation on total defense, preparedness and crisis planning

[4561] The existing Nordic defense cooperation within NORDEFCO serves as a model for Nordic political and military cooperation

[4562] In 2018, a new vision for NORDEFCO towards 2025 was adopted

[4563] The vision states that the Nordic countries should work towards being able to cooperate in “peace, crisis and conflict”

[4564] The vision has an associated action plan with 16 specific goals that encompass several possible areas of cooperation, including total defense, civil-military cooperation, and resilience against complex threats

[4567] Cooperation within the UN The UN has a key role in coordinating humanitarian responses to natural disasters and complex crises

[4568] This work is mainly coordinated by the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA

[4569] A successful humanitarian response requires close cooperation between UN agencies, other international organizations, including in particular the EU, voluntary organizations, military actors and national authorities

[4570] The Government's overall goal is to support the UN's coordinating role in humanitarian crises to ensure an effective response

[4571] Cooperation between the UN and the EU in disaster response is constantly increasing in scope

[4572] To avoid duplication of systems and capacities, it has been important to have a clear division of responsibilities between these two organizations, something Norway has supported

[4573] In 2015, the member states of the UN adopted a global framework for disaster prevention, the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030, which Norway has also joined and committed to following up on

[4574] The overall goal of the Sendai Framework is to prevent and reduce risk

[4575] The framework shall promote societal security locally, nationally, and internationally through cross-sectoral cooperation, and operationalized through seven sub-goals: – reduce mortality from incidents and disasters

[4576] Reduce the number of people affected by incidents and disasters

[4577] globally by 2030. – reduce economic losses resulting from adverse events as a share of gross national product

[4578] – reduce the loss of critical infrastructure and critical societal functions, including education and health

[4579] by 2030. – increase the number of countries that have national and local strategies for social security by 2020. – increase international development cooperation through appropriate and sustainable assistance that supports countries’ own plans for implementing this framework

[4580] by 2030. – strengthen systems for (early) warning and risk information to the population

[4581] The work is coordinated by the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR

[4582] The Directorate for Civil Protection and Emergency Preparedness (DSB) is the national contact point for the Sendai Framework and coordinates the national follow-up

[4583] The UN Sustainable Development Goals for 2030 were adopted before the Sendai Framework (autumn

[4584] The Sustainable Development Goals see the environment, economy and social development in context, and can function as a roadmap when it comes to linking initiatives coming from various UN organizations, including the Sendai Framework for Disaster Reduction

[4585] There is therefore synergy between the two instruments for sustainability goals and disaster prevention

[4586] The UN has stated that the Sendai Framework will help to complement the monitoring of some of the sustainability goals

[4587] This applies in particular to the goals related to poverty eradication, sustainable, safe and resilient cities/settlements, as well as stopping climate change and combating its consequences

[4588] The states' own work on risk management and assessments of future risk conditions provides predictability with regard to what needs to be secured and how it can be done

[4589] This is something that has a direct impact on the living conditions of the population

[4590] It is therefore important that Norwegian agencies and institutions that participate in various UN forums/arenas actively contribute to seeing the connections between the various initiatives being taken, and to clarify the benefits for the individual country

[4591] Particularly important is the work on guidelines to understand such connections and that work is carried out across the different sectors that have responsibility within these two areas (sustainability goals and disaster prevention

[4700] Social Security

[4701] in an uncertain world Appendix

[4702] Social security work as a chain In order to facilitate a systematic approach to social security work, the Government sees the work as a continuous chain consisting of the links of prevention, preparedness, management, recovery and learning

[4703] In all links of the chain, knowledge building and adaptation to changes in the risk and vulnerability picture are an integral part of the work

[4704] Prevention is about taking measures to reduce the possibility of an unwanted event, or to reduce the consequences of a possible event in advance

[4705] Prevention of undesirable events caused by accidents and natural events differs from prevention of intentional acts

[4706] Behind an intentional unwanted action is a threat actor who has actively set out to cause harm

[4707] This places special demands on the planning, design and implementation of risk-reducing measures

[4708] For some unwanted incidents, we have good knowledge of cause-and-effect relationships that can provide a basis for targeted preventive measures

[4709] Emergency preparedness is about planning and preparing measures that strengthen the ability to handle unwanted incidents so that the extent of damage is kept to a minimum

[4710] The ability to act quickly can be crucial to the extent of damage an incident will cause

[4711] Preparedness capability is governed, among other things, by access to resources and materials that can help to handle the incident quickly

[4712] Other factors that are important for preparedness are the interoperability that is built through exercises and updated plans

[4713] Exercises provide knowledge about one's own skills, procedures, resources and how other actors work

[4714] Handling is about translating preparedness into efforts and collaboration

[4715] In incident management, time is often critical

[4716] Good incident management therefore requires that those who are to handle the crisis have the necessary resources in the form of equipment and personnel, and that they have the necessary authority to handle the situation quickly

[4717] Collaboration between different actors with specialized capabilities related to personnel, expertise and material is important, especially in complex incidents

[4718] Recovery is about the ability to make lost functions work again after an event

[4719] When the handling of an incident comes to an end, the task becomes gradually to restore normalcy

[4720] High recovery capacity in the form of an overview of resources, established routines, good expertise and repair readiness helps to increase society's resilience

[4721] In the short term, the ability to implement temporary adaptations that restore parts of the functionality may be important

[4722] Figure 1.1 Social security work as a chain

[4723] Social security in an uncertain world Learning

[4724] Learning from exercises and incidents is important to improve the ability to handle future incidents

[4725] Learning from exercises and incidents requires good evaluations and the ability to implement improvement measures

[4726] Based on Report

[4727] St. 10 (2016–2017) Risk in a safe society

[4728] Act (2016–2017) introduced requirements for follow-up of findings from incidents and exercises within the area of ​​public security in the civil sector in the state administration

[4729] For the ministries, the requirement has been included in the social security instructions

[4730] For state enterprises on the civilian side, the requirements are incorporated into relevant governance documents

[4731] More about the Ministry of Justice and Public Security's coordination role Sectoral responsibility facilitates professional specialization and division of labor, but at the same time creates a need for coordination

[4732] Coordination is necessary to – Ensure uniform and harmonized social security work across sectors

[4733] – Avoid gray areas and clarify the division of responsibilities for overlapping areas

[4734] – Ensure coherent and integrated measures and instruments

[4735] – Be able to set cross-sectoral priorities at the national level

[4736] – Manage interdependencies, including dependencies between critical societal functions

[4737] – Ensure efficient utilization of society's collective resources

[4738] Support effective crisis management on the civilian side

[4739] As stated in the Royal Resolution on the Responsibility for Civil Security and the Civil Security Instructions, the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness has a general coordination role to ensure a comprehensive and coordinated national preparedness, across all civil sectors and critical societal functions

[4740] The Ministry shall safeguard the overall nature of the government's policy and be a driving force that ensures that the field of social security receives the necessary attention and priority

[4741] The coordination role has been established because coordination often requires a coordinating body that has primary responsibility for ensuring that coordination takes place, that has the competence to make decisions, and that has the ability to weigh up different interests and considerations

[4742] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security is responsible for various coordination matters, and the coordination role is supported by a wide range of activities, see table

[4758] Societal security in an uncertain world

[4759] Basic principles The national civil protection work is based on the basic principles of responsibility, equality, proximity and cooperation. – The principle of responsibility, which means that the organization that is responsible for a subject area in a normal situation is also responsible for the necessary emergency preparedness preparations and for handling extraordinary incidents in the area

[4760] The responsible body must decide what is an acceptable risk. – The principle of similarity, which means that the organization one operates with during crises should initially be as similar as possible to the organization one has on a daily basis

[4761] – The subsidiarity principle, which means that crises should be handled organizationally at the lowest possible level

[4762] – The principle of cooperation, which means that authorities, businesses or agencies have an independent responsibility to ensure the best possible cooperation with relevant actors and businesses in the work of prevention, preparedness and crisis management

[4763] The Storting's plenary session sets important frameworks for military and civil preparedness, for example through emergency preparedness legislation and the annual budget decisions

[4764] Important foreign and security policy, defense policy and emergency preparedness issues are handled by the Extended Foreign and Defense Committee (DUUFK

[4765] The committee consists of the ordinary members of the Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee, the President of the Storting and the leaders of the party groups

[4766] The chair convenes the committee when he or she deems it necessary, or when the Prime Minister, the Minister for Foreign Affairs or one third of the committee members request it

[4767] The same applies when the Minister of Defence requests it in important emergency preparedness issues, or when the Minister of Justice and Emergency Preparedness requests a discussion of issues regarding terrorist preparedness

[4768] The negotiations in UUFK are secret unless otherwise expressly decided

[4769] The Government has the ultimate responsibility for preparedness in Norway, including the overall political responsibility for both the management and handling of preventive preparedness work and crises that arise

[4770] The government is addressing a number of emergency preparedness issues, both through the budget process and in discussions of issues in government conferences

[4771] According to our state customs, each minister has constitutional responsibility in his or her area, within the laws and appropriations granted by the Storting

[4772] This means that the individual minister retains his constitutional responsibility even in a crisis situation

[4773] If the Prime Minister so wishes, a matter may, instead of being considered in plenary session in the government, be considered in the Government Security Committee (RSU

[4774] The RSU consists of the Prime Minister, the Minister of Justice and Emergency Situations, the Minister of Defense, the Minister of Finance and the Minister of Foreign Affairs

[4775] In addition, other ministers may be invited if the matters affect their areas of responsibility

[4776] RSU will primarily be relevant for matters of defense, security policy or emergency nature where the content indicates limited dissemination of information

[4777] In some cases, it will follow from the Constitution, legislation or decision-making regulations that necessary formal decisions must be made by the government through a resolution of the King in Council

[4778] This applies, for example, to crises that are of such a serious nature that it is appropriate to implement powers in accordance with emergency legislation, submit proposals to the Storting, or declare command authority for Norwegian military forces

[4779] A significant degree of flexibility is planned when it comes to organizing the work

[4780] In many situations, it will be appropriate for civil servants from affected ministries and affected agency heads to participate in meetings in the government, RSU and the Crisis Council, see discussion below

[4781] Social security in an uncertain world

[4782] The Prime Minister leads and coordinates the work of the Government

[4783] These are tasks the Prime Minister would also have in a crisis situation

[4784] The Prime Minister will also play a central role in external communication, contact with other countries' heads of government, international organizations, parliamentary leaders in the Storting, the Royal House, etc

[4785] The Prime Minister's involvement in each crisis will depend on the nature and scope of the crisis

[4786] In crises that fall within the scope of the Emergency Preparedness Act, the Prime Minister has been delegated special powers in situations where it is imperative to make decisions to safeguard society's interests

[4787] The Prime Minister's Office must plan so that the Prime Minister and the Government can carry out their duties even in crisis situations

[4788] The Prime Minister's Office also performs tasks as secretariat for government conferences, the Norwegian Council of State and the King in Council

[4789] The Prime Minister's Office must be able to provide administrative support, secretarial functions and contribute with advice

[4790] The ministries The administrative system for central crisis management builds on the basic principles of societal security

[4791] This means that the ministry that is responsible for a sector on a daily basis is also responsible for emergency planning and measures in a crisis situation

[4792] In the event of crises, the ministries will obtain situation reports from their own operational agencies and identify and make decisions about necessary measures within their own areas of responsibility to handle the current situation

[4793] They will prepare the basis for decision-making and facilitate overall political clarifications where necessary

[4794] The ministries must be able to handle communication with the media and the public

[4795] The work must be coordinated with other ministries, especially the ministry designated as the lead ministry

[4796] The departments must ensure that operational actors have the necessary authorizations, so that the need for processing at the government level does not delay the handling of acute situations where there is a danger to life, health or major loss of material assets

[4797] The Crisis Council is the highest administrative coordination body at the ministry level, and was established to strengthen central coordination

[4798] The council has six permanent members

[4799] the government councillor at the Prime Minister's Office, the foreign affairs councillor at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the ministerial councillors at the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, the Ministry of Defence, the Ministry of Health and Care Services and the Ministry of Local Government and Modernisation, respectively

[4800] If necessary, the council can be expanded to include all other ministries, and representatives of underlying agencies and special expertise environments

[4801] All ministries can take the initiative to convene the Crisis Council

[4802] The leadership department chairs the council's meetings

[4803] If a lead ministry has not been decided, the council will be led by the Ministry of Justice and Public Security

[4804] The crisis council is also used beyond handling crises and major incidents, as a system of administrative meetings has been established

[4805] It has been appropriate for the purpose of discussing and anchoring overall emergency preparedness and crisis management challenges and reviewing relevant incidents and exercises

[4806] However, the actual processing of such cases takes place in the ordinary manner within the line of the responsible ministry

[4807] Lead Ministry

[4808] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security is the permanent lead ministry in civil national crises, unless otherwise determined

[4809] The Ministry's coordination responsibility and responsibility for the bulk of the civil rescue and emergency preparedness resources in Norway means that the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness will always have a central role in most cross-sectoral national crises

[4810] In some situations, and when it comes to incidents that primarily affect one sector, it will be natural for someone other than the Ministry of Justice and Public Security to hold the lead department role

[4811] The Crisis Council is authorized by the government to decide which ministry will be the lead ministry in a particular crisis

[4812] In case of doubt or disagreement in the Crisis Council, the choice of the lead ministry is decided by the Prime Minister in consultation with the ministers concerned

[4813] The appointment of a lead ministry does not entail changes in constitutional responsibilities, and all ministries retain responsibility and decision-making authority for their respective areas of responsibility

[4814] In a crisis situation, the lead ministry shall, among other things: – prepare and distribute overall situation reports, including on the basis of reports

[4815] St. 5 2020–2021 Societal security in an uncertain world obtained information from other ministries, reports from operational agencies and the media image – identify and assess the need for measures at a strategic level – coordinate that necessary measures within one's own area of ​​responsibility are implemented, and ensure necessary coordination with other ministries and agencies – ensure that coordinated information is provided to the media and the population Crisis Support Unit and the Civil Situation Centre in the Ministry of Justice and Public Security

[4816] The Crisis Support Unit (KSE) shall support the management department and the Crisis Council in their coordination functions and is the permanent secretariat for the Crisis Council

[4817] KSE has expertise in strategic crisis management, as well as capacities in the form of infrastructure, such as mobile technical solutions

[4818] KSE can, upon request, assist other ministries with personnel support in their crisis management

[4819] KSE also supports the Ministry of Justice and Public Security's coordination role in the area of public security and public security

[4820] This includes contributions to training activities, as well as advice and guidance on crisis management to the ministries

[4821] The Civil Situation Centre is organised as part of KSE, and is a permanent point of contact for information to and from the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness in the event of extraordinary incidents and crises

[4822] Through the transition to a 24-hour manned presence in the Civil Situation Centre in 2014, the capacity for timely warning and analysis of the situational picture, as a basis for necessary decisions in crises, was significantly strengthened
